item.title: Intensity-controlled Raster Scanning Carbon Ion Radiation Therapy With a Heavy-ion Gantry: Clinical Experience at Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center.
item.dc:creator: Dvornikovich K, Held T, Franke H, Cakir C, Dörsam L, Manzey T, Jiang ZC, Winter S, Sittinger M, Winter M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Dvornikovich K, Held T, Franke H, Cakir C, Dörsam L, Manzey T, Jiang ZC, Winter S, Sittinger M, Winter M, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.09.003
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43044650



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Carbon ions have biophysical advantages over photons, including a finite range, increased relative biological effectiveness, and lowered oxygen dependence. Maximum treatment flexibility is attainable with rotational beam delivery. We report our clinical experience using the carbon-ion gantry at the Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center with intensity-controlled raster scanning capability, focusing on treatment toxicity. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A total of 1622 patients treated using the carbon-ion gantry between 2012 and 2026 were evaluated. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Toxicity analysis was conducted using Common Terminology Criteria of Adverse Events v5.0. RESULTS: The median age preradiation therapy was 59 years (range, 18-91). Most patients had locally advanced tumors (21.8% T4; 11.2% T3) without regional lymph node metastases (45.4% N0). The most common treatment indications were sacrococcygeal tumors (n = 331; 20.4%), followed by tumors of the paranasal sinuses (n = 166; 10.2%) and the spine (n = 121; 7.5%). A total of 486 patients (30.0%) received carbon-ion reirradiation, the most frequent carbon-ion gantry treatment indication viewed across all patients. The most common particle therapy beam-angle number was 2 (range, 1-7). The use of more than 2 beam angles was particularly frequent in tumors of the skull base (45.8%) and the thoracic region (40.0%). High-grade (III and IV) acute and late toxicity rates were 2.4% and 4.2% in primary treatment. Mean numbers of acute and late grade I and II toxicity events per patient were 2.2 (95% confidence interval, 2.0-2.4) and 2.0 (95% confidence interval, 1.7-2.4), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Carbon-ion radiation therapy using a heavy-ion gantry resulted in favorable toxicity rates in specific indications. Further interdisciplinary research demonstrating the clinical benefit of carbon-ion radiation therapy is required. This study provides more evidence supporting particle therapy facilities and may serve as a foundation for prospective clinical trials.

item.title: Allogeneic umbilical cord-mesenchymal stem/stromal cells for chronic radiation-induced xerostomia: a phase I study with multimodal functional and imaging assessment.
item.dc:creator: Švajger U, Mitrovič G, Hartman K, Ležaić L, Kokalj M, Plavc G, Prešeren U, Blatnik O, Bavec A, Sočan A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Švajger U, Mitrovič G, Hartman K, Ležaić L, Kokalj M, Plavc G, Prešeren U, Blatnik O, Bavec A, Sočan A, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.10.058
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43067442



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Radiation-induced xerostomia is a clinically significant adverse effect of head and neck radiotherapy with limited treatment options. This prospective, single-arm case series evaluated the safety, feasibility, and exploratory clinical efficacy of ultrasound-guided intraglandular administration of allogeneic umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (UC-MSCs) in patients with chronic radiation-induced xerostomia. METHODS AND MATERIALS: Ten disease-free survivors of oropharyngeal cancer with CTCAE grade 2-3 xerostomia received ultrasound-guided UC-MSC injections into both parotid and submandibular glands. Each parotid gland received 50 × 10⁶ UC-MSCs and each submandibular gland 25 × 10⁶ UC-MSCs. Safety was the primary outcome. Exploratory assessments were performed at baseline and at 1 and 4 months and included patient-reported outcome measures, unstimulated and stimulated salivary flow rates, salivary biochemical analyses, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound shear-wave elastography, salivary gland scintigraphy, and, where feasible, core-needle biopsy. RESULTS: No serious adverse events were observed. Procedure-related effects were limited to transient injection-site pain, swelling, and local discomfort. Objective salivary flow rates and most biochemical parameters remained stable throughout follow-up. In contrast, patient-reported outcomes improved, with the greatest changes at 4 months. Xerostomia Questionnaire scores decreased from 63.44 ± 16.81 at baseline to 53.18 ± 21.16 at 4 months (p = 0.0066), and visual analogue scale scores from 64.65 ± 17.30 to 60.29 ± 18.11 (p = 0.0122). Improvements were also observed in xerostomia and sticky saliva domains of the EORTC QLQ-H&N35. MRI showed only subtle changes in T2-weighted signal intensity ratios, while elastography remained unchanged. Scintigraphy demonstrated increased excretion velocity at 4 months (p = 0.0355). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-arm case series of 10 patients, ultrasound-guided intraglandular UC-MSC administration was feasible and well tolerated over four months, with no serious adverse events. Improvements in PROMs and scintigraphic excretion velocity were exploratory findings in the absence of a control group and occurred despite largely unchanged salivary flow. Clinical efficacy remains to be established in adequately powered, randomized, placebo-controlled trials.

item.title: Characterization of the peri-tumoral immune infiltrate at the invasive front of oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Beck CR, Sotov V, Pfister TD, Jozaghi Y, Hyrcza M, Stone SC, Smith SM, AlGhamdi D, Mifsud M, Verma N, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Beck CR, Sotov V, Pfister TD, Jozaghi Y, Hyrcza M, Stone SC, Smith SM, AlGhamdi D, Mifsud M, Verma N, et al.
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108157
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43067119



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objectives were to determine the association between high peri-tumoral immune infiltrate (PTII) and survival, determine the association between cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and PTII and to characterize immune cell density at the invasive front of oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC). METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 303 patients with OCSCC were categorized into low and high PTII on whole block sections using histopathological grading. A tissue microarray from the retrospective cohort was used to assess percentage of stroma staining for alpha smooth muscle actin (aSMA)/(CAFs). Next, multiplex immunohistochemistry was used on the whole block section to stain immune cell sub-populations to characterize high vs low PTII (10 cases, 10 controls). RESULT: Multivariate Cox regression showed high-PTII was associated with better distant (HR = 0.2,CI:0.06-0.93,p < 0.04) and regional control (HR = 0.26,CI:0.08-0.81,p < 0.02) as well as overall survival (HR = 0.41,CI: 0.23-0.72,p < 0.04). Multivariate logistic regression showed higher percent of αSMA/(CAF) positive stroma had a negative association with high PTII (OR = 0.94,CI: 0.91-0.98;p < 0.0014) suggesting a biological relationship. The case-control cohort showed significantly higher cellular density in the high-PTII group, 4859 cells/mm2 vs 1984 cells/mm2 (p < 0.001). The high-PTII stroma and tumor had a higher cellular density of helper T cells (p < 0.01), cytotoxic T cells (p < 0.01) The high-PTII stroma had higher M1 macrophages (p < 0.05)/PDL1 + M1 macrophages (p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: High peri-tumoral immune infiltrate (PTII) assessed on whole block sections at the invasive front was associated with improved patient survival, and decreased CAFs. Patient with high-PTII showed significantly higher stromal infiltration of Helper and Cytotoxic T cells, and M1 macrophages (PD-L1 + ).

item.title: Association between statin use and postoperative recurrence in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis: a single-center retrospective observational study.
item.dc:creator: Sasaki G, Kondo K, Fushimi N, Nomura F
item.description:
Authors: Sasaki G, Kondo K, Fushimi N, Nomura F
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10818-4
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43066758



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS), a type 2-dominant form of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, is characterized by frequent postoperative relapse. Although statins exhibit pleiotropic anti-inflammatory and profibrinolytic properties that may mitigate impaired fibrinolysis in ECRS, their clinical impact remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between statin use and postoperative recurrence in patients with ECRS undergoing functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS). METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, observational study included patients diagnosed with ECRS according to the Japanese Epidemiological Survey of Refractory Eosinophilic Chronic Rhinosinusitis criteria who underwent FESS between April 2015 and December 2025. Postoperative recurrence was defined as the need for any of the following treatment escalations: revision surgery, systemic oral corticosteroid therapy, local triamcinolone administration, or use of (or eligibility for) biologic therapy. RESULTS: Forty-nine patients completed at least 6 months of follow-up, including 11 statin users (22.4%). Statin users were significantly older than non-users (60.9 vs. 52.3 years; p=0.033), whereas other baseline characteristics were comparable. Statin use was associated with lower odds of overall postoperative recurrence (27.3% vs. 63.2%; OR 0.22; 95% CI 0.05-0.96; p=0.046). In exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for age and asthma, the association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (adjusted OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.06-1.32; p=0.115). CONCLUSION: Statin use was associated with lower odds of overall postoperative recurrence in patients with ECRS. However, this association was attenuated after adjustment for age and asthma and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Larger prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

item.title: Pretreatment total gross tumor volume complements TNM staging in predicting survival in locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Delikaya M, Özkaya Akagündüz Ö, Hazeral YZ, Esassolak M
item.description:
Authors: Delikaya M, Özkaya Akagündüz Ö, Hazeral YZ, Esassolak M
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10827-3
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43066757



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the prognostic significance of pretreatment gross tumor volume (GTV) and determine whether volumetric assessment provides additional prognostic value beyond conventional TNM staging in patients with locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with definitive radiotherapy, predominantly with concurrent systemic therapy. METHODS: This retrospective study included 124 patients treated with definitive radiotherapy between 2012 and 2024; 117 received concurrent systemic therapy. Pretreatment GTVprimary, GTVnodal, and GTVtotal were measured on planning CT for patients treated with upfront radiotherapy and on the CT component of pre-induction PET/CT for patients receiving induction chemotherapy. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to determine cutoff values. Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. The incremental prognostic value of volumetric parameters was assessed using Akaike's Information Criterion (AIC)-based model comparison. RESULTS: The selected cutoff value for GTVtotal was 36 cc. Although GTVprimary showed the highest AUC in ROC analysis, GTVtotal remained associated with disease-specific survival after multivariable adjustment and yielded the lowest AIC among the compared models. Patients with GTVtotal > 36 cc had poorer disease-specific survival. GTVtotal, T stage, and age > 60 years were independently associated with disease-specific survival. CONCLUSION: Pretreatment GTVtotal provides complementary prognostic information beyond conventional TNM staging and may improve risk stratification in patients with locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with definitive radiotherapy, predominantly with concurrent systemic therapy. The data-derived cutoff requires external validation before clinical use. The 36-cc threshold may be influenced by the predominance of hypopharyngeal tumors in the high-volume group and should be applied cautiously to laryngeal cancer cohorts.

item.title: Sentinel lymph node biopsy using ICG-[99mTc]Tc-nanocolloid and superselective level I dissection.
item.dc:creator: Heldens GTN, Weijs WLJ, Arens AIJ, van Rijk MC, Janssen MJR, van Engen-van Grunsven I, Honings J, Coppen C, Verhoeven T, Takes RP
item.description:
Authors: Heldens GTN, Weijs WLJ, Arens AIJ, van Rijk MC, Janssen MJR, van Engen-van Grunsven I, Honings J, Coppen C, Verhoeven T, Takes RP
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10735-6
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43066755



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is a widely used diagnostic procedure for early-stage oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) in Europe. While SLNB generally demonstrates high sensitivity, previous studies have reported lower sensitivity in floor of mouth squamous cell carcinoma (FOMSCC). However, earlier studies used only radioactive tracers. European guidelines now recommend combining a fluorescent tracer with superselective neck dissection (SSND) of level I for FOMSCC. This study evaluates the sensitivity of SLNB using a hybrid ICG-[99mTc]Tc-nanocolloid tracer combined with level I SSND. MATERIALS & METHODS: From 2016 to 2023, prospective data on SLNB were collected from patients with cT1-2N0M0 OSCC. Staging included ultrasound, with fine needle aspiration for suspicious nodes, and CT or MRI as indicated. SLNB was performed using ICG-[99mTc]Tc-nanocolloid, planar lymphoscintigraphy, and SPECT/CT. In FOMSCC cases, SSND of level Ia and the preglandular triangle of Ib was performed. RESULTS: A total of 144 patients were included: 92 cT1 and 52 cT2 tumours, with 87 tongue, 22 floor of mouth, and 35 other subsites. Median follow-up was 40 months. Metastatic lymph nodes were detected in 39 patients (27.1%). Isolated regional recurrence was observed in 6 patients (4.2%). The overall sensitivity of SLNB was 86.7%, with a negative predictive value of 94.3%. Among the 22 FOMSCC patients, no isolated regional recurrence occurred, resulting in both sensitivity and negative predictive values of 100%. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that a state-of-the-art SLNB protocol using a hybrid tracer and level I SSND achieves high sensitivity, including in FOMSCC cases.

item.title: Minor Salivary Gland Tumors: Clinicopathologic Characteristics, Survival Outcomes, and AJCC Version 9 T-Category Migration in a 16-Year Single-Center Cohort.
item.dc:creator: Akalın M, Zorlu ME, Rustamli E, Öğüt B, Sert A, Düzlü M, Aydil U, Yılmaz M
item.description:
Authors: Akalın M, Zorlu ME, Rustamli E, Öğüt B, Sert A, Düzlü M, Aydil U, Yılmaz M
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10730-x
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43066753



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the clinicopathological features and long-term outcomes of minor salivary gland tumors and evaluate stage migration and survival stratification after restaging malignant tumors according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) version 9. METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients treated for primary minor salivary gland tumors from January 2010 to January 2026. All tumors underwent descriptive analysis; malignancies were restaged under the AJCC eighth edition and Version 9 and analyzed for survival. Kaplan-Meier estimates and log-rank tests assessed overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and disease-specific survival (DSS). RESULTS: Of 72 patients, 40 (55.6%) had malignancies. The hard palate predominated; pleomorphic adenoma was the most common diagnosis and adenoid cystic carcinoma the predominant malignancy. Median follow-up for malignant cases was 109 months; 5-year OS, RFS, and DSS were 69.1%, 85.0%, and 77.7%, respectively. Version 9 changed pT in six patients (15.0%; five upstaged and one downstaged), shifting the dichotomized T1-T2/T3-T4 distribution from 20/20 to 17/23. Version 9 significantly stratified OS and DSS (p = 0.024 and p = 0.028), whereas the eighth-edition grouping did not (p = 0.075 and p = 0.176); neither system stratified RFS. Nodal involvement was associated with poorer OS and DSS (both p < 0.001), perineural invasion with poorer OS (p = 0.031), and positive margins with poorer RFS (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: AJCC Version 9 produced clinically relevant T-category migration and significantly stratified OS and DSS in this cohort. In univariable analyses, nodal involvement was associated with poorer OS and DSS, perineural invasion with poorer OS, and positive surgical margins with poorer RFS. Larger studies using complete stage groups and formal model-performance measures are needed to confirm these findings.

item.title: Unraveling the molecular basis of salivary gland cancer: Recent progress, diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications - a narrative review, part II.
item.dc:creator: Di Santo D, van Waterschoot J, Meulemans J, Hauben E, Willaert R, van Mierlo A, Cremasco A, Ferrarotto R, Skálová A, Stenman G, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Di Santo D, van Waterschoot J, Meulemans J, Hauben E, Willaert R, van Mierlo A, Cremasco A, Ferrarotto R, Skálová A, Stenman G, et al.
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10820-w
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43066752



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Salivary gland cancers (SGC) are rare and heterogeneous, exhibiting markedly diverse biological behavior and clinical courses. This, together with their generally poor response rates to systemic chemotherapy, has driven research into specific and/or recurrent genetic alterations that may have diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance. This review provides an overview of current knowledge concerning the molecular basis of SGC. METHODS: A comprehensive review of the literature from the last 15 years was performed, focusing on molecular alterations and targeted therapeutic approaches in the following salivary gland carcinomas: salivary duct carcinoma (SDC), myoepithelial carcinoma (MECA), polymorphous adenocarcinoma (PAC), carcinoma ex-pleomorphic adenoma (CXPA), and other more rare histological subtypes. RESULTS: Current insights into the clinical and pathogenetic significance of genetic alterations in SGC are presented, their diagnostic and prognostic relevance is discussed, and available targeted therapies are reviewed. SDC is characterized by overexpression of the androgen receptor (AR) in nearly all cases and is HER2 positive in up to 50% of the cases; targeted therapies directed against both AR and HER2 are available. MECA is a fusion-positive cancer, frequently with fusion​s involving PLAG1, while in PAC, molecular alterations typically involve the PRKD genes. However, targeted treatments are still lacking for both entities. CXPA should be treated according to the specific subtype. CONCLUSION: A deeper understanding of the molecular pathogenesis of SGCs may enable refined diagnosis, more precise definition of prognostic subtypes, and identification of tumor-specific targets for personalized therapies.

item.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists in idiopathic subglottic stenosis: patient attitudes, barriers, facilitators and patient-reported outcomes.
item.dc:creator: Gosselin LE, Anderson C, Al Yaghchi C
item.description:
Authors: Gosselin LE, Anderson C, Al Yaghchi C
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10835-3
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43066751



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) is a rare disease of unknown etiology. There has been a growing interest within the patient community regarding the potential therapeutic role of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) in the management of iSGS, potentially through weight loss-mediated or direct anti-inflammatory mechanisms. The objective of this study was to evaluate patient perspectives and attitudes regarding the potential role of GLP-1 RA in the overall management of iSGS. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional observational study through a structured online anonymous survey. The survey comprised 53 items organized across four domains: demographics; attitudes, barriers and facilitators to GLP-1 RA use; therapy details and adverse effects; and perceived therapeutic impact. RESULTS: A total of 1382 patients with iSGS completed the survey. Diagnostic delay of iSGS was a prominent finding, with patients reporting a substantial lag between symptom onset and confirmed diagnosis. Overall, 407 patients used GLP-1 RA therapy. Among GLP-1 RA users, 38.44% self-reported perceived improvement in airway symptoms. Key barriers to GLP-1 RA therapy included cost, access, and limited physician awareness. Thematic analysis of the patient's responses revealed patients' attitudes toward GLP-1 RA therapy were largely favorable, with patients citing anti-inflammatory benefits and quality of life improvements as primary motivators for use. CONCLUSION: GLP-1 receptor agonists are generally viewed favorably by patients with iSGS. Patient-reported experiences suggest possible improvements in airway symptoms, although prospective studies are required to establish causality and clarify mechanistic benefit.

item.title: Clinical-pathological nodal discordance and survival outcomes in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Chang CW, Liao LJ, Hung CY, Cheng PC, Cheng YP, Chiang CJ, Lee WC, Hsu WL, Chen TC
item.description:
Authors: Chang CW, Liao LJ, Hung CY, Cheng PC, Cheng YP, Chiang CJ, Lee WC, Hsu WL, Chen TC
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108233
Published: 2026-Nov-20
PMID: 43063685



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of discordance between clinical and pathological nodal staging in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains poorly understood. This study investigates how clinical-pathological nodal discordance impacts survival outcomes in OSCC. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 14,618 OSCC patients from the Taiwan Cancer Registry who underwent primary surgical resection with neck dissection between 2018 and 2022. Patients were stratified into four groups: true negative (cN0pN0), occult metastasis (cN0pN + ), overt metastasis (cN + pN + ), and false positive (cN + pN0). Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, propensity score matching, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. RESULTS: Among 14,618 patients, 7,154 (48.9 %) were true negative, 1,290 (8.8 %) had occult metastasis, 3,197 (21.9 %) had overt metastasis, and 2,977 (20.4 %) were false positive. Approximately 30 % of patients presented with clinical-pathological discordance in neck staging. Despite harboring more advanced T-stage primary tumors, false-positive patients achieved survival outcomes comparable to those of true-negative patients (5-year DFS 71.6 % vs. 71.3 %; OS 76.1 % vs. 75.8 %). Extranodal extension (ENE) was present in 25.5 % of occult metastasis patients and 53.2 % of overt metastasis patients. Regardless of occult or overt presentation, the presence of ENE dictated similarly poor survival outcomes compared with patients without ENE (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Clinical-pathological nodal discordance is common in OSCC, and ENE, rather than the clinical detectability of nodal disease, is the dominant prognostic factor in node-positive disease. Elective neck dissection therefore serves a dual diagnostic and therapeutic role, identifying occult metastases that elude preoperative imaging and improving long-term survival.

item.title: Cancer risk with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists: An umbrella review of meta-analyses.
item.dc:creator: Petrelli F, Meregalli G, Berzi D, Nicolì F, Viglino F, Della Pepa G, Indovina F, Dalmiglio C, Forloni F, Bossi A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Petrelli F, Meregalli G, Berzi D, Nicolì F, Viglino F, Della Pepa G, Indovina F, Dalmiglio C, Forloni F, Bossi A, et al.
Journal: Cancer epidemiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.canep.2026.103273
Published: 2026-Nov-20
PMID: 43063527



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for diabetes and obesity is increasing, but effects on uncommon or long-latency cancers are uncertain. We synthesised meta-analytic evidence for overall and site-specific cancer risk and assessed methodological quality, overlap, outcome-level certainty, and credibility. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 30 June 2026 for meta-analyses of GLP-1RAs or the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide and incident cancer. Randomised and observational evidence was considered separately; review-level estimates were not recombined. We assessed methodological confidence with AMSTAR 2, overlap with corrected covered area (CCA), outcome-level certainty with a GRADE-informed algorithm, and association credibility with Ioannidis criteria. FINDINGS: We included 38 meta-analyses from 2012 to 2026. The most comprehensive placebo-controlled randomised evidence (48 trials, 94 245 participants, median follow-up 70 weeks) showed no statistically significant association with thyroid cancer (odds ratio [OR] 1·37, 95% CI 0·82-2·31; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 treated), pancreatic cancer (0·84, 0·53-1·35), colorectal cancer (1·11, 0·75-1·65), or breast cancer (0·95, 0·60-1·49), and no overall cancer increase (OR 1·05, 0·98-1·13 across 50 trials). Thyroid and agent-specific haematological signals were inconsistent or based on sparse events; between-review discordance for thyroid and colorectal cancer was largely attributable to comparator restriction, choice of estimator, and handling of zero-event trials rather than to differences in cancer ascertainment. Observational syntheses suggested lower hepatocellular carcinoma risk (hazard ratio 0·60, 95% CI 0·41-0·88), but four reviews had very high overlap (CCA 50·0%). Outcome-level certainty was moderate for five outcomes, low for 11, and very low for five; none was high. No association met class I or II credibility criteria. INTERPRETATION: Randomised evidence shows no evidence of a material increase in overall or site-specific cancer risk over currently observed trial durations (median about 70 weeks, maximum about 5 years), and cancer concerns alone do not justify withholding indicated GLP-1RA treatment. Small, rare, long-latency, dose-specific, or agent-specific effects cannot be excluded, and the evidence cannot address exposure beyond approximately five years, well short of the 8-10 years generally required to evaluate cancer incidence. Observational protective associations should not support causal or cancer-prevention claims. FUNDING: None.

item.title: Effects of proton pump inhibitors on serum and fecal biomarkers and intestinal microbiota in dogs.
item.dc:creator: Romano FS, Barbosa IS, Melchert A, Amaral AR, Vendramini THA, Suchodolski J, Lallo MA
item.description:
Authors: Romano FS, Barbosa IS, Melchert A, Amaral AR, Vendramini THA, Suchodolski J, Lallo MA
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361194
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43063192



Abstract:
The gastrointestinal tract of mammals, including dogs and cats, is inhabited by a highly diverse intestinal microbiota that plays an essential role in both health and disease. This microbial ecosystem influences various processes such as metabolism, immunity, neurodevelopment, and the maintenance of homeostasis and can be altered in many circumstances such as diseases, the use of oral medications and gastrointestinal pH. Proton Pump Inhibitors are suspected of causing dysbiosis due to the alteration of gastric pH. This study evaluated the effects PPIs on the microbiota of healthy dogs. Twenty Golden Retrievers were randomly allocated into four treatment groups (n = 5 per group): Omeprazole (OMP - 1 mg/kg twice a day), Esomeprazole (ESO - 1 mg/kg twice a day), Lansoprazole (LSP - 0.5 mg/kg twice a day), and Control (Placebo, CTL) and treated for 30 days. Feces were collected at the beginning (T0) and end (T30) of the trial for evaluation of dysbiosis index and blood biochemistry was performed to quantify target variables of gastrointestinal diseases (folate, cobalamin, iron and calcium) at the same period. Gastrin serum concentrations were evaluated at T0 and T30 only for the LSP group. Results showed no clinical signs or changes in the global dysbiosis index among treatments. However, specific microbial alterations were observed, including a reduction in Turicibacter in the OMP and ESO groups, and an increase in Streptococcus spp. in few individuals in the OMP group. Serum biomarkers related to inflammation and gastrointestinal absorption remained unchanged. In this study, PPIs did not induce intestinal dysbiosis or caused any clinical impairment, although some isolated microbial changes were noted.

item.title: Influence of peri-implant soft tissue thickness on marginal bone loss following immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla: A retrospective comparative study.
item.dc:creator: Kadkhodazadeh M, Alam M, Golkar M, Naghshbandi T
item.description:
Authors: Kadkhodazadeh M, Alam M, Golkar M, Naghshbandi T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360723
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43063175



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marginal bone stability is a critical determinant of the long-term success and esthetic harmony of dental implants. Peri-implant soft tissue thickness (STT) has been proposed as a biological factor influencing crestal bone remodeling. This retrospective comparative study aimed to evaluate the relationship between peri-implant STT and marginal bone loss (MBL) following immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla after one year of functional loading. METHODS: Fifty immediate implant sites from 50 patients were retrospectively analyzed. Based on mid-buccal soft tissue measurement, implants were classified as thin (STT ≤ 1 mm; n = 22) or thick (STT > 1 mm; n = 28) phenotypes. Clinical parameters, including probing depth, bleeding on probing, plaque index, keratinized tissue width, and pink esthetic score, and radiographic parameters (MBL) were extracted from patient records. MBL was measured on standardized periapical digital radiographs taken immediately after surgery and at one-year follow-up using a custom positioning index. RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 57.88 ± 11.16 years. MBL was significantly higher in the thin soft tissue group (1.34 ± 0.19 mm) compared with the thick tissue group (1.00 ± 0.20 mm; p < 0.0001). STT exhibited a strong negative correlation with MBL (r = -0.749, p < 0.0001). Other variables showed no significant intergroup differences. No significant difference in MBL was observed between implant systems. CONCLUSION: Within the limitations of this retrospective study, peri-implant soft tissue thickness was identified as a key determinant of marginal bone preservation after immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla. Thicker mucosa was associated with significantly reduced bone resorption and more stable peri-implant esthetic outcomes after one year.

item.title: Induction Immunochemotherapy Followed by Definitive Chemoradiotherapy and Consolidation Immunotherapy for Locally Advanced Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Prospective Phase II Study.

item.description:
Authors: Lin L, Li H, Song X, Zhao L, Cheng Y, Liu M, Yu W, Zhang Q, Cai X, Yang Y, et al.
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70828
Published: 2026-Nov-19

Abstract:
Long-term survival after definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (dCCRT) remains limited in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). We evaluated induction immunochemotherapy followed by dCCRT and consolidation immunotherapy in this setting. This prospective, single-arm Phase II study enrolled 54 adults selected for definitive nonsurgical treatment. The planned regimen comprised two cycles of induction immunochemotherapy with nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin, and a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor, followed by dCCRT with 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions and concurrent weekly chemotherapy. The same PD-1 inhibitor was planned as consolidation therapy for up to 1 year. The primary endpoint was the 2-year overall survival (OS) rate. Fifty-three patients (98.1%) completed two induction cycles, all 54 proceeded to dCCRT, and 31 (57.4%) received consolidation immunotherapy. Among all 54 enrolled patients, the 2-year OS and progression-free survival (PFS) rates were 84.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 75.2%-95.0%) and 61.5% (95% CI, 49.5%-76.4%), respectively, after a median follow-up of 28.1 months. Adverse events occurred predominantly during dCCRT and were mainly hematologic; lymphopenia and esophagitis were among the most frequent toxicities. Exploratory analyses suggested that suboptimal response after induction immunochemotherapy was associated with shorter PFS. The survival outcomes observed with this sequential approach support further evaluation of its comparative clinical benefit in randomized studies. item.title: Rethinking Oncologic Trismus: Evidence for an Undermeasured Soft Tissue Phenotype.

Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70559
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43059079



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Soft tissue impairment spanning the lymphedema-fibrosis continuum and trismus are highly prevalent head and neck cancer toxicities. While fibrosis is often implicated in trismus, no prior study has directly examined the association between clinician-graded head and neck lymphedema and fibrosis (HNL/F) and maximal interincisal opening (MIO). METHODS: HNL/F classifications and MIO were evaluated in 832 cancer survivors at a specialized Trismus Clinic (2020-2025). Spearman's correlation, ANOVA, univariate, and multivariate linear regression examined HNL/F-MIO relationships overall and by region (face, neck, and intraoral). RESULTS: In unadjusted and adjusted analyses, all clinician-graded HNL/F classifications in the face were significantly associated with reduced MIO. In all regions, fibrosis was associated with reduced MIO in unadjusted models; after covariate adjustment, fibrosis remained significant, except in the neck. CONCLUSION: These findings provide the first evidence linking regional and severity-based HNL/F classification with MIO and support HNL/F phenotyping in trismus assessment.

item.title: Standardization and pitfalls of iENE in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: Optimizing diagnostic accuracy, prognostic staging and treatment selection.
item.dc:creator: De Felice F, Goanta L, Marchi F, Succo G, Maroldi R, Sanguineti G
item.description:
Authors: De Felice F, Goanta L, Marchi F, Succo G, Maroldi R, Sanguineti G
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108237
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43057067



Abstract:
Extranodal extension (ENE) represents the cornerstone of adverse nodal staging in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). While pathological ENE (pENE) is the historical benchmark, the clinical push toward non-surgical primary organ preservation and surgical de-escalation has forced reliance on imaging-derived ENE (iENE). However, applying iENE to clinical decision-making introduces significant methodological and clinical dilemmas. Inspired by recent insights from radiotherapy de-intensification trials in oncology, where "less is not simple" and non-superiority is frequently misconstrued as non-inferiority, this critical review evaluates the evolution of iENE. We critically analyze the transition from unstandardized radiological reporting - "the pre-consensus era" - to international consensus frameworks - "the standardized reporting era" -, dissect the trade-offs between sensitivity, specificity, and disease prevalence and evaluate the incorporation of iENE into the 9th Edition UICC/AJCC TNM staging system. Ultimately, we distinguish the utility of iENE across three distinct clinical objectives: identifying pathological ENE, predicting oncological outcomes for staging and selecting patients for surgery versus chemoradiotherapy.

item.title: Targeting the IGF-estrogen receptor signaling nexus in thyroid cancer: From molecular crosstalk to precision therapeutics.
item.dc:creator: Margoni A, Papavassiliou KA, Papavassiliou AG
item.description:
Authors: Margoni A, Papavassiliou KA, Papavassiliou AG
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108234
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43057066



Abstract:
The potential convergence of insulin-like growth factor (IGF) and estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) signaling represents a compelling molecular hypothesis in thyroid cancer, linking growth factor and hormonal responsiveness to malignant progression and therapeutic resistance. IGF signaling through IGF-1 receptor (IGF-1R) and insulin receptor isoform A (IR-A) activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-AKT-mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways, promoting proliferation and survival. An experimentally established IGF-2/IR-A autocrine loop further contributes to tumor-cell proliferation and impaired differentiation. Concurrently, ERα fosters proliferative and invasive phenotypes through keratin 19 (KRT19), potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 3 (KCNQ3)-associated MAPK activation, and epigenetic regulation, whereas estrogen receptor beta (ERβ) may exert context-dependent antiproliferative effects. Although reciprocal ERα-IGF-1R interactions have been demonstrated in non-thyroid models, direct molecular crosstalk in thyroid cancer remains unconfirmed. These findings provide a rationale for investigating ERα antagonism or degradation, selective ERβ activation, and IGF axis inhibition as potential therapeutic strategies. This article proposes that functional interplay between IGF and ERα signaling may create distinct oncogenic dependencies beyond the individual contributions of either pathway. Establishing such cooperation and determining whether combined inhibition offers advantages over individual targeting are essential steps toward evaluating its potential for biomarker-guided therapeutic development in thyroid cancer.

item.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Survival in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Hunter AE, Uralov D, Byrd MC, Cannon TY, Curry J, Osazuwa-Peters N
item.description:
Authors: Hunter AE, Uralov D, Byrd MC, Cannon TY, Curry J, Osazuwa-Peters N
Journal: JAMA otolaryngology-- head & neck surgery | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoto.2026.3648
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43056129



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Metformin has known metabolic effects and associated survival benefits in head and neck cancer. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) also modulate systemic metabolism through regulating blood glucose levels and lipid metabolism. OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether GLP-1RAs are associated with survival outcomes in patients with head and neck cancers. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using clinical data from January 1, 1990, through December 1, 2025, from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults with histologically confirmed head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC) were included. Data were analyzed in January 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was overall survival for all HNSCC and stratified by site. The secondary outcome was overall survival among patients concurrently using GLP-1RAs and metformin. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) with 95% CIs were estimated. RESULTS: There were 4532 patients (mean [SD] age, 63.4 [10.9] years; 1638 female individuals [36.1%] and 2891 male individuals [63.8%]) included in the cohort. Across all subsites, GLP-1RA users had significantly improved overall survival compared with controls at 1-year (aHR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.36-0.49), 3-year (aHR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.43-0.54), and 5-year intervals (aHR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.46-0.57). By anatomic subsite, GLP-1RA use remained consistently associated with a lower hazard of mortality at 5-year intervals (oral cavity: aHR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.51-0.70; oropharynx: aHR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.41-0.64; larynx: aHR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39-0.61). We also observed significant overall survival among patients who used GLP-1RAs and metformin at 1 year (aHR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.23-0.36), 3 years (aHR, 0.36; 95% CI, 0.30-0.42) and 5 years (aHR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.34-0.45). CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this cohort study suggest that there may be survival benefits associated with GLP-1RA use among patients with HNSCC across several subsites. Future prospective and interventional studies of GLP-1RA potential metabolic adjuncts in oncologic care may help corroborate the associations from this retrospective study.

item.title: Integrating genetic and lung tissue proteomics data to identify susceptibility proteins for lung cancer.
item.dc:creator: Xu S, Shi J, Shu XO, Tao R, Dou Y, Guo X, Wen W, Yang Y, Zhang B, Wu J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Xu S, Shi J, Shu XO, Tao R, Dou Y, Guo X, Wen W, Yang Y, Zhang B, Wu J, et al.
Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute | DOI: 10.1093/jnci/djag424
Published: 2026-Nov-19
PMID: 43055353



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proteins directly impact disease development and act as drug targets. We integrated genetic and lung tissue proteomic data to identify lung cancer susceptibility proteins and evaluated them as candidate drug targets. METHOD: We profiled the proteome and genome in 200 non-neoplastic lung tissue samples and constructed genetic models to predict protein abundance. These models were applied to genome-wide association study (GWAS) data of 55,174 lung cancer cases and 1,294,174 controls to evaluate associations between predicted abundance and lung cancer risk overall and by major histological subtypes. Independent lung tissue proteomic data was used for cross-dataset evaluation, followed by colocalization and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization. Prioritized proteins were cross-referenced against drug databases. RESULTS: We identified 29 lung cancer risk-associated proteins at a false discovery rate < 5%, including 25 for overall lung cancer, two (AQP3 and IL18) specific to adenocarcinoma, and two (HMGN2 and HLA-DMB) specific to squamous cell carcinoma. Genes encoding 15 proteins are located > 2Mb away from known GWAS risk loci. Among the remaining 14 proteins at known risk loci, five (EPHX2, CLDN18, PSMD5, ARHGAP27, and CYP2S1) showed associations independent of proximal lead variant. Of the 29 proteins, eight were predicted and six were significant in independent data. DSP, IL18 and TYMP proteins demonstrated both reproducible and potential causal evidence and are targeted by six drugs that are FDA-approved or in phase III trials. CONCLUSION: Our study identified novel lung cancer susceptibility proteins and potential therapeutic targets, offering insights into lung cancer biology and informing future translational research.

item.title: Tissue and blood-based biomarkers of immunotherapy response in head and neck Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Stouras I, Zazas E, Rocca MC, Ansarin M, Psyrri A
item.description:
Authors: Stouras I, Zazas E, Rocca MC, Ansarin M, Psyrri A
Journal: Cancer treatment reviews | DOI: 10.1016/j.ctrv.2026.103247
Published: 2026-Nov-18
PMID: 43067175



Abstract:
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment landscape of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). In the recurrent/metastatic (R/M) setting, pembrolizumab has been approved as first-line therapy, either alone for tumors with PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) ≥ 1 or in combination with platinum-based chemotherapy regardless of PD-L1 CPS status. Moreover, both pembrolizumab and nivolumab have been approved as monotherapy in platinum-refractory disease. More recently, perioperative pembrolizumab received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for resectable, locally advanced HNSCC with PD-L1 CPS ≥ 1 following encouraging results of the KEYNOTE-689 trial. Although PD-L1 CPS is the only validated HNSCC-specific biomarker for immunotherapy selection, its accuracy remains limited, as response rates are modest even among PD-L1 CPS-high patients, while some tumors with low/negative CPS may still derive benefit. This underscores the need for novel biomarkers with greater predictive value that can serve as more precise selection and risk stratification tools for patients with HNSCC considering immunotherapy. Recent studies have investigated several biomarkers of immunotherapy outcomes in HNSCC in both tissue and blood, paving the way toward adopting non-invasive approaches. In this review, we aim to summarize recent advances in ICI biomarker discovery in non-nasopharyngeal HNSCC and to set the basis for the adoption of an integrated approach, comprising both tissue-based and liquid biomarkers.

item.title: Local and distant site definitive treatment in metastatic oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: A national cancer database analysis.
item.dc:creator: West JD, Lin ME, Ziltzer RS, Ulloa R, Kim I, Swanson MS
item.description:
Authors: West JD, Lin ME, Ziltzer RS, Ulloa R, Kim I, Swanson MS
Journal: American journal of otolaryngology | DOI: 10.1016/j.amjoto.2026.104986
Published: 2026-Nov-18
PMID: 43063590



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Assess effect of local and distant site definitive treatment on overall survival (OS) in patients receiving chemotherapy for metastatic oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (M1 OPSCC). METHODS: Adult M1 OPSCC patients treated with chemotherapy (2010-2017) were identified via the National Cancer Database. Primary outcomes were median and 3-year OS, stratified by HPV status. The primary predictor was additional definitive treatment target: local site (LST), distant site (DST), or both (LDST). Pairwise and Kaplan-Meier log-rank tests and multivariable Cox regression assessed the impact of treatment site on OS by HPV status. Multiple imputation addressed incomplete HPV data. RESULTS: Of 2684 patients, 70.3% had missing HPV status; five imputed datasets were generated. LST was the most common additional treatment (61.7%). Combined local and distant treatment (LDST) yielded the highest median survival overall (24.1 months) and in both HPV-positive (27.7 months) and HPV-negative (18.1 months) subgroups. Pairwise log-rank comparisons showed any additional definitive treatment improved 3-year OS regardless of HPV status. On multivariate regression controlling for clinical characteristics, LDST reduced 3-year mortality risk versus DST alone in both HPV-positive (HR = 0.60, 95% CI 0.50-0.70, p < 0.0001) and HPV-negative (HR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.58-0.75, p < 0.0001) disease. CONCLUSIONS: In this NCDB analysis, adding definitive treatment to chemotherapy in M1 OPSCC is associated with improved overall survival. Although our study is limited by selection bias and limited retrospective data in small sample sizes, our findings suggest that further prospective investigation should be considered to determine whether definitive treatment is warranted in select patients undergoing chemotherapy to improve locoregional control.

item.title: Megestrol Acetate for Prevention of Weight Loss During Modern Radiotherapy in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.dc:creator: Muangwong P, Samakgarn V, Malasri P, Toapichattrakul P, Chitapanarux I
item.description:
Authors: Muangwong P, Samakgarn V, Malasri P, Toapichattrakul P, Chitapanarux I
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70558
Published: 2026-Nov-18
PMID: 43053594



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weight loss is a common complication during radiotherapy for head and neck cancer and may adversely affect treatment tolerance and outcomes. We evaluated whether megestrol acetate (MA) prevents treatment-related weight loss. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label randomized controlled trial, 102 patients with non-nasopharyngeal head and neck squamous cell carcinoma undergoing radiotherapy were assigned to MA plus standard care or standard care alone. Standard care consisted of nutritional counseling, symptom management, and feeding-tube placement when clinically indicated. The primary endpoint was change in body weight from baseline to 6 weeks post-radiotherapy. RESULTS: At 6 weeks post-radiotherapy, the MA group showed a mean weight gain of 2.07 kg, whereas the control group lost 1.74 kg (p < 0.01). Weight gain was primarily due to increased fat mass, with no significant difference in muscle mass. Quality of life was similar between groups. CONCLUSION: MA improved weight preservation during radiotherapy and may serve as an adjunct to supportive care in head and neck cancer. Published: 2026-Nov-18

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate changes in basal serum cortisol levels in patients with atrophic-erosive oral lichen planus (OLP) and oral lichenoid lesion (OLL) treated with 0.5% triamcinolone acetonide mouthrinses and to assess the occurrence of clinical manifestations associated with adrenal dysfunction. METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted in 68 patients with clinically and histopathologically confirmed atrophic-erosive OLP or OLL. Participants received 0.5% triamcinolone acetonide mouthrinses following a tapering regimen over 3 months. Basal serum cortisol levels were measured at baseline, after 30 days, and after 90 days of treatment. Clinical and demographic variables and treatment-related adverse effects were analyzed. RESULTS: Mean basal serum cortisol levels decreased from 17.05 ± 4.38 μg/dL at baseline to 8.79 ± 7.34 μg/dL after 1 month of treatment. Following dose tapering, serum cortisol levels (SCL) partially recovered to 11.94 ± 6.44 μg/dL at 3 months. No clinical manifestations of adrenal insufficiency were observed. Baseline SCL were significantly associated with serum cortisol concentrations after 1 month (r = 0.34; p < 0.05). Older patients exhibited smaller hormonal fluctuations during treatment. CONCLUSIONS: Triamcinolone acetonide induced a transient reduction in SCL without clinically relevant adrenal dysfunction, suggesting a limited systemic impact when administered a tapering regimen.

item.title: Turkish Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Oral Health-Related Quality of Life Measure for Children/Adolescents With Down Syndrome (OH-QOLADS).

item.description:
Authors: Tanrıverdi M, Zengin Yazıcı G, Güney Yılmaz G, Uygur Şahin T

Published: 2026-Nov-18

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to adapt the Oral Health-Related Quality of Life for Adolescents with Down Syndrome (OH-QOLADS) scale into Turkish and evaluate its psychometric properties. It also explored oral health status and quality of life among children with Down syndrome (DS). METHODS: The study included 100 children with DS and their mothers. Sociodemographic and oral health data were collected through structured questionnaires. The OH-QOLADS, comprising child and family forms with two timeframes, was translated and culturally adapted following international guidelines. Internal consistency, CFA, and item-total correlations were conducted to assess psychometric validity. RESULTS: The Turkish OH-QOLADS showed excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α and McDonald's ω > 0.94) across all forms and timeframes. CFA supported the original four-factor structure (symptoms/functioning, emotional well-being, social participation, and family impact) with strong model fit indices (CFI > 0.98; RMSEA < 0.05). Most participants reported poor oral health, low tooth brushing frequency, and minimal preventive care. Oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) scores were significantly associated with comorbidities like thyroid disease, diabetes, and hearing impairments. CONCLUSION: The Turkish OH-QOLADS is a valid, reliable tool for assessing OHRQoL in children with DS. The findings highlight the need for better access to preventive dental services and caregiver support.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of worldwide prevalence of geographic tongue (GT) in healthy children and adolescents. METHODS: A search was conducted in five main databases (MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, and Global Index Medicus), two gray literature sources (ProQuest and Google Scholar), and hand search up to August 31, 2025, for studies related to GT in subjects up to 19 years of age. item.title: Characteristics and Survival of Patients with Primary and Secondary Distant Metastasis of Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OPSCC).
item.dc:creator: McGarrah PW, Agwaze RN, O'Byrne J, Abdel-Halim C, Fazer-Posorske CA, Fuentes Bayne HE, Neben Wittich MA, Lester SC, Routman DM, Ma DJ, et al.

Authors: McGarrah PW, Agwaze RN, O'Byrne J, Abdel-Halim C, Fazer-Posorske CA, Fuentes Bayne HE, Neben Wittich MA, Lester SC, Routman DM, Ma DJ, et al.
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag449
Published: 2026-Nov-18
PMID: 43053275



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 20% of patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) develop distant metastases (DM). Survival outcomes after DM vary widely depending on clinical and biologic factors. This study compared baseline characteristics, management strategies, and oncologic outcomes among OPSCC patients with primary and secondary DM to better inform prognostication and therapeutic planning. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients treated at a tertiary care center with HPV/p16-positive, HPV/p16-negative, or unknown-status OPSCC who developed DM at any point. Treatments included surgery, radiation, and systemic therapy delivered with curative or non-curative intent. Cohort characteristics and overall survival (OS), stratified by primary versus secondary DM and treatment subgroups, were assessed using chi-square tests and Kaplan Meier analyses. RESULTS: A total of 132 patients were included: 18 with primary DM and 114 with secondary DM. HPV-positivity was lower in primary versus secondary DM group (22.2% vs 75.4%). Median follow-up was 32.4 months. Median OS from DM diagnosis was significantly shorter for primary versus secondary DM (9.6 vs 20.4 months; HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.16-3.46). Patients with secondary DM were more likely to receive metastasis-directed therapy (MDT). Median OS was 56.4 months with MDT and 13.2 months without (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.23-0.61). CONCLUSIONS: This is the largest single center analysis of DM OPSCC to date. Primary DM OPSCC was associated with worse survival and lower HPV-positivity. Patients with DM, particularly those with HPV-positive disease, may achieve extended survival following aggressive treatment such as MDT.

item.title: Prognostic Value of Adverse Pathological Features in Early-Stage Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: de Castro LCM, Silva WPS, Macedo MSR, de Castro RB, Pereira-Filho FJF, Meneses WEF, Nogueira TNAG, Matos LL, Kowalski LP, da Fonseca MSR, et al.
item.description:
Authors: de Castro LCM, Silva WPS, Macedo MSR, de Castro RB, Pereira-Filho FJF, Meneses WEF, Nogueira TNAG, Matos LL, Kowalski LP, da Fonseca MSR, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70556
Published: 2026-Nov-18
PMID: 43051928



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depth of invasion, perineural invasion, lymphovascular invasion, and worst pattern of invasion (WPOI) increasingly guide management of early-stage oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC), yet their prognostic value across clinically relevant outcomes remains incompletely synthesized. We systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed their association with nodal metastasis, recurrence, and survival. METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and trial registries were searched for cohort studies of these predictors in surgically treated early-stage OCSCC (T1-T2N0M0). Study quality was assessed and data extracted per PRISMA 2020. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed when outcomes were compatible, with sensitivity analyses restricted to multivariable estimates and to alternative harmonization choices. Certainty of evidence was graded using GRADE. RESULTS: Forty studies (15 674 patients) met inclusion criteria; 30 were meta-analyzed. Perineural invasion was associated with worse disease-free survival (HR: 2.23, 95% CI: 1.80-2.77), recurrence, and nodal metastasis (OR: 4.06, 95% CI: 2.22-7.42). Depth of invasion, lymphovascular invasion, and WPOI were associated with nodal metastasis (ORs 2.92, 3.11, and 5.68, respectively), with widely overlapping confidence intervals across predictors; associations with survival outcomes were imprecise. Certainty of evidence was moderate at best and low or very low for most associations. CONCLUSIONS: Perineural invasion, depth of invasion, lymphovascular invasion, and WPOI were each associated with adverse outcomes in early-stage OCSCC, particularly nodal metastasis. These estimates derive from heterogeneous retrospective studies and do not allow ranking of the predictors against one another. Prospective studies with standardized definitions and adjusted analyses are needed.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, and their combination increase the rate of spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women undergoing induction of labour. DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled, 2×2 factorial phase 3 trial (SAINT). SETTING: 11 Norwegian hospitals providing comprehensive obstetric care. PARTICIPANTS: Nulliparous women aged 18-50 years with a singleton live fetus in cephalic presentation at term with an indication for induction of labour. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to oral sodium bicarbonate (4×1 g per dose) plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide (20 mg per dose), oral sodium bicarbonate plus intravenous placebo, oral placebo plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide, or double placebo. The investigational medicinal product was administered at the onset of active labour and repeated every four hours to a maximum of three doses. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Spontaneous vaginal birth (no instrumental or caesarean delivery). RESULTS: Between 4 January 2023 and 29 January 2025, 3094 nulliparous women were randomised, and 2963 comprised the full analysis set. Spontaneous vaginal birth occurred in 57% (422/741) in the bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide arm, 61% (445/734) in the bicarbonate arm, 61% (449/741) in the hyoscine butylbromide arm, and 56% (422/747) in the double placebo arm. Marginal risk differences for spontaneous vaginal birth compared with double placebo were -0.2 (95% confidence interval -5.1 to 4.7; P=0.93) percentage points for combined treatment, 3.1 (-1.7 to 8.0; P=0.21) percentage points for bicarbonate, and 4.0 (-0.8 to 8.9; P=0.10) percentage points for hyoscine butylbromide. Serious adverse events were similar between groups, and no treatment related serious morbidity or deaths were observed. CONCLUSIONS: No clear evidence was found that intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, or their combination increased spontaneous vaginal birth compared with placebo. Although small beneficial effects cannot be excluded, the findings do not support routine intrapartum use of either agent to facilitate spontaneous vaginal birth after induction of labour. Abstract:
PURPOSE: To report a single arm multi-site phase II study evaluating a reduced contralateral neck elective nodal clinical target volume (enCTV) in p16+ oropharyngeal cancer (p16+OPC). METHODS AND MATERIALS: Newly diagnosed p16+OPC without contralateral nodal involvement but with clinical or pathological features warranting contralateral elective nodal treatment were eligible. Treatment included proton- or photon-based definitive (chemo)radiation or adjuvant (chemo)radiation following Transoral Robotic Surgery. All patients received SAVER enCTV and the primary endpoint was two-year elective out-of-field contralateral nodal failure. Dosimetric comparison between SAVER enCTV and consensus enCTV of the first 10 definitive and adjuvant patients was performed. Overall survival (OS), progression-free-survival (PFS), toxicities, and patient reported outcomes were analyzed. RESULTS: Fifty-two patients were enrolled, of which 36 (69.2%) received definitive (chemo)radiation. Thirty-five (67.3%) had bulky or multiple ipsilateral lymph nodes and 18 (34.6%) had significant smoking history. With median follow-up of 31.0 months (range 13 - 49 months), there were no contralateral nodal failures with an upper limit one-sided 95% confidence interval for contralateral nodal failure of 2.7%. Two-year OS and PFS were 92.2% (95% CI [88.5 - 95.9%]) and 86.2% (95% CI [81.4 - 91.0%]), respectively. Acute grade 3 toxicity was observed in 13 (25%) patients including 8 (15.4%) who received a gastrostomy tube. There were no grade 4-5 toxicities. CONCLUSION: Selective avoidance of nodal volumes at minimal risk in the N0 contralateral neck can be safely performed while maintaining excellent regional control in the definitive and adjuvant settings. Dose to contralateral organs at risk and toxicity outcomes were favorable.

item.title: Intrapartum oral azithromycin versus placebo alone or in combination with other antimicrobials on maternal infection in South East Asia.
item.dc:creator: Patel AB, Kurhe K, Bhargav S, Khedikar V, Waikar M, Shivkumar P, Goudar SS, Metgud MC, Kavi A, Derman R, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Patel AB, Kurhe K, Bhargav S, Khedikar V, Waikar M, Shivkumar P, Goudar SS, Metgud MC, Kavi A, Derman R, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0346359
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43050477



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: In low-resource facilities that routinely use intrapartum prophylactic antimicrobials, the use of multiple antimicrobials could be rationalised by a single oral dose of oral azithromycin. METHODS: The Azithromycin Prevention in Labor Use Study (A-PLUS), a randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled trial performed across eight sites in seven countries amongst women who planned to deliver vaginally. They were randomly assigned to receive study drug, a single intrapartum 2 gm oral dose of azithromycin or an identical appearing placebo. Data from four South-East Asia sites (Indian sites Nagpur and Belagavi, Pakistan, and Bangladesh) was analyzed to evaluate whether the use of non-study antimicrobials (alone or in-combination) given after randomization through one-day postpartum for any indication (prophylactic or treatment) modified the effect of study drugs on maternal outcomes (maternal infections, antibiotic usage 2-42days postpartum on ambulatory basis or re-hospitalization). The non-study antimicrobials given after randomization through 1-day postpartum was defined by four exposure sub-groups within azithromycin and placebo arm as, Use of: i) No non-study antibiotic; ii) Cephalosporin only; iii) Other non-study non-cephalosporin antibiotics; and iv) Cephalosporin and other non-study non-cephalosporin antibiotics. An intent to treat (ITT) analysis was adopted. Adjusted relative risks and 95% confidence intervals comparing azithromycin with placebo were estimated using Poisson regression models with robust variance estimators that included study site, maternal non-study antimicrobial use, and a treatment-by-non-study antimicrobial use interaction term. RESULTS: All maternal non-study antibiotic subgroups had balanced randomization between azithromycin and placebo. The risk of any maternal infections was reduced when only azithromycin was received versus placebo (RR = 0.75; 95% CI-0.57-0.98) and when group iv antimicrobials were used with azithromycin compared to only group iv antimicrobials (RR = 0.79; 95% CI-0.66-0.95). The use of antibiotics from day2-42 was similar in both arms (azithromycin or placebo) with or without use of other antimicrobials. CONCLUSIONS: This secondary analysis found no evidence that non-study antimicrobials use modified the effect of azithromycin on maternal outcomes. This study underscores the importance of considering an easily administrable intrapartum prophylaxis of oral monotherapy in low resource, high risk for infections sites to reduce antimicrobial resistance due to multiple antimicrobial use.

item.title: Preclinical safety evaluation of Vernolac, a commercially available polyherbal nutraceutical comprising Vernonia zeylanica, Nigella sativa, Hemidesmus indicus, Smilax glabra, and Leucas zeylanica, in Wistar rats.

Authors: Wijerathne SK, Epitawala Arachchige OV, De Vass Gunawardane S, Kothalawala A, Dissanayake TL, Ranaweera G, Murugananthan A, Galhena P, Senathilake K, Samarakoon SR

Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
Vernolac is a commercially available polyherbal formulation comprising Vernonia zeylanica aerial parts, Nigella sativa seeds, Hemidesmus indicus roots, Smilax glabra rhizome, and Leucas zeylanica aerial parts. Although previous in vitro studies have demonstrated the anticancer potential of Vernolac and its active ingredients, safety data are available only for some of the plant ingredients of Vernolac. In the present study, acute and 28-day repeat-dose toxicity of Vernolac were evaluated in Wistar rats in accordance with OECD guidelines 420 and 407, respectively. Acute toxicity was investigated for 14 days after administering a single oral dose of 2000 mg/kg to 10 animals (5 males, 5 females). A repeat-dose toxicity study was conducted, in which the human equivalent therapeutic dose in rats (HED; 165 mg/kg/day), a mid-dose (2 × HED; 330 mg/kg/day), and a high dose (4 × HED; 660 mg/kg/day) were administered to three separate groups, each comprising 10 naive animals (5 males and 5 females), for a period of 28 days. In both acute and repeat-dose studies, no morbidity, mortality, changes in food and water intake, relative organ weights, microscopic changes in organs, hematological changes, or clinical signs of toxicity were observed. In the acute study, a significant increase in AST and ALT levels was observed in males. In the 28-day repeated dose study, a significant reduction in ALT was observed only in females receiving 4x HED. In summary, the LD50 of Vernolac is above 2000 mg/kg, and a dose up to two times the therapeutic daily dose is non-toxic in Wistar rats over 28 days. The liver may be a target organ of toxicity when overdosed.

item.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of Jordanian mothers regarding acute gastroenteritis in children.
item.dc:creator: Al-Shboul MA, Ahmad AM, Khashroom MT, Almugheed SN, Alramahi AE, Al-Zoubi ZM, Al-Essa DH, Namir RM
item.description:
Authors: Al-Shboul MA, Ahmad AM, Khashroom MT, Almugheed SN, Alramahi AE, Al-Zoubi ZM, Al-Essa DH, Namir RM
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362841
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices of mothers living in Jordan regarding childhood acute gastroenteritis and to identify factors associated with poor knowledge, poor practice, lack of oral rehydration solution (ORS) awareness, and antibiotic use without medical consultation. METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 730 mothers living in Jordan using a structured Arabic-language questionnaire. Participants were recruited through paediatric hospital settings and social media using convenience sampling. Composite knowledge and practice scores were calculated, and four multivariable binary logistic-regression models were fitted to examine factors associated with the prespecified outcomes. RESULTS: The mean composite knowledge score was 15.73 ± 6.83 out of 28, corresponding to 56.18% of the maximum score, and 31.37% of participants were categorized as having poor knowledge. The mean composite practice score was 4.58 ± 1.71 out of 10, corresponding to 45.84% of the maximum score, and 61.23% were categorized as having poor practice. Overall, 54.52% identified three or fewer of the eight dehydration signs assessed, 59.59% were aware of ORS, and 3.15% selected ORS as their intended first action. Compared with residence in Central Jordan, residence in North Jordan was associated with higher adjusted odds of poor knowledge (aOR 2.18, 95% CI 1.38-3.45), poor practice (aOR 1.74, 95% CI 1.19-2.55), lack of ORS awareness (aOR 1.52, 95% CI 1.01-2.28), and antibiotic use without medical consultation (aOR 1.81, 95% CI 1.12-2.91). University-level education was associated with lower odds of poor knowledge and poor practice, while healthcare employment was associated with lower odds of poor practice and lack of ORS awareness. CONCLUSION: Important gaps were identified in dehydration-sign recognition, ORS-related intended practices, and overall reported home-management practices. These findings support the development and evaluation of targeted caregiver-education initiatives emphasizing dehydration recognition, appropriate ORS use, safe medication practices, and timely care-seeking. Regional and educational differences may help identify groups requiring additional support; however, the observed associations should not be interpreted causally because of the cross-sectional design.

item.title: Behavioural sleep quality and quantity and their associations with age, salivary cortisol and abnormal behaviours: A preliminary field study in racing thoroughbreds.
item.dc:creator: Hennes N, Greening L, McBride S, Lemarchand J, Cognié J, Foury A, Phelipon R, Bourguignon H, Ruet A, Lansade L
item.description:
Authors: Hennes N, Greening L, McBride S, Lemarchand J, Cognié J, Foury A, Phelipon R, Bourguignon H, Ruet A, Lansade L
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0342874
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43050441



Abstract:
Sleep plays a key role in both physical recovery and welfare. However, sleep patterns remain poorly documented in animals, particularly in athletic horses. This study aimed to provide a detailed description of sleep quantity and quality in training Thoroughbred racehorses and to investigate their relationships with age, abnormal behaviours, and cortisol. Thirteen Thoroughbreds (2-7 years old) were continuously monitored in their home environment for 48 hours. An ethogram was used to quantify sleep-related behaviours associated with the two main behavioural sleep states: non-rapid eye movement (NREM-like) and rapid eye movement (REM-like), as well as sleep interruptions (from day 1 at 12:00 to day 3 at 12:00). Sleep Quality Indices (SQIs), reflecting the relationship between sleep duration and sleep interruptions (SIs), were then calculated. Behavioural observations of four indicators of poor welfare (alertness, stereotypies, inactivity, aggressiveness towards humans) were performed using scan sampling, and salivary cortisol was measured each morning. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess the links between sleep quantity and quality, age, mean cortisol, and abnormal behaviours. Age was significantly associated with behavioural sleep quantity, being positively associated with total behavioural NREM-related sleep (Wald test: χ2 = 5.40, p = 0.02), and negatively associated with total behavioural REM-related sleep (Wald test: χ2 = 4.36, p = 0.04) and total recumbency duration (Wald test: χ2 = 5.68, p = 0.02). Morning cortisol concentrations were negatively associated with Total SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 5.26, p = 0.02) and Combined SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 5.60, p = 0.02). Likewise, horses displaying abnormal behaviours more frequently had lower Total SQI (Wald test: χ2 = 4.07, p = 0.04), pointing to a potential link between stress or altered welfare and poorer sleep quality. These findings suggest that, whilst the type and duration of equine behavioural-related sleep may be mainly affected by age, sleep quality is associated with both cortisol levels and the expression of abnormal behaviours, indicating that poor sleep quality may be linked to poor welfare in this population of horses. Overall, these findings highlight behavioural sleep quality as a potential component of racehorse welfare assessment and warrant further investigation into the factors influencing sleep in athletic horses.

Abstract:
This multicenter case-control study assessed (2019-2023) the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil. Eligible cases were adults (≥ 18 years) with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx. Controls (cancer-free individuals) were matched a posteriori by region, sex, and age. Oral, genital, and anal samples were collected and processed at a central laboratory for HPV genotyping. Oral HPV prevalence was similar between cases and controls (14% vs. 12%), predominantly involving high-risk genotypes (35 out of 40); HPV-16/18 was more prevalent among cases (7.3% vs. 1.9%; p = 0.024), with most HPV-16/18-positive cancers located in the oropharynx (10 out of 11). Genital HPV prevalence was 39% with no case-control differences, while anal HPV prevalence was 17%. Cases were more frequently positive for any high-risk anal HPV type than controls (16% vs. 9%; p = 0.049). Minimal genotype concordance was observed between oral and anogenital sites. Current smokers had ten-fold higher odds of being cases (adjustedOR 10.0; 95% CI 2.92-34.6). Oral HPV-16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer (adjustedOR 6.30; 95% CI 1.52-26.1). Multisite HPV genotyping revealed site-specific colonization patterns, with genital infections being most prevalent among both men and women. After multivariable adjustment, only oral HPV-16/18 infection was strongly associated with head and neck cancer, especially oropharyngeal carcinoma.

item.title: Multicenter CT-Based Deep Learning for Preoperative Nodal Risk Stratification in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.

item.description:
Authors: Xu S, Yan X, Su Y, Qi J, Chen X, Li Y, Xiong H, Jiang J, Wei Z, Chen Z, et al.

Published: 2026-Nov-18

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate preoperative risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains difficult. We developed and validated ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model using preoperative computed tomography (CT), and explored related biological features in multi-omics analyses. METHODS: A total of 1560 patients with PTC from six hospitals were retrospectively included. The Tongji Hospital cohort was divided into training and internal validation sets, and five external cohorts were used for independent testing. Seven 2.5D tumor slices were extracted per patient, encoded with a DenseNet201 backbone, and fused by a Transformer. Model performance was compared with radiomics, ensemble learning, and multi-instance learning using AUC, calibration, decision curve, and precision-recall analyses. Bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics were used to explore related biological features. RESULTS: ThyLNT achieved an AUC of 0.882 (CI, 0.858-0.905) in the training cohort, 0.787 (CI, 0.738-0.835) in the internal validation cohort, and 0.772 (CI, 0.662-0.878) to 0.827 (CI, 0.763-0.885) across the five external cohorts. It showed multicenter discrimination, whereas calibration and threshold-dependent operating characteristics varied across cohorts. Multi-omics analyses provided exploratory biological context, including candidate associations with vascular endothelial growth factor A-related signaling and lipid metabolism. CONCLUSIONS: ThyLNT demonstrated multicenter performance for preoperative LNM prediction in PTC and may support risk stratification, although calibration, threshold use, and clinical utility require prospective validation.

item.title: Impact of positional obstructive sleep apnea phenotype on mandibular advancement therapy outcomes: A multicenter cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Nicoletti S, De Virgilio A, Terranova S, Brunori M, Vicini C, Campisi R, De Ceglie V, Casale M, Moffa A, Maniaci A, et al.
