Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43056883



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Mandibular advancement devices (MADs) are an established treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but reliable predictors of response remain limited. Positional OSA (POSA) has been proposed as a favorable phenotype. This study evaluated whether positional phenotype influences respiratory outcomes and treatment success in patients treated with MAD. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 82 consecutive patients with OSA treated with MAD across six tertiary sleep centers. Baseline and follow-up home sleep apnea tests performed at least 6 months after completion of MAD titration were analyzed. POSA was defined according to Cartwright's criteria as a supine apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) at least twice the non-supine AHI. Outcomes included changes in respiratory parameters and treatment success according to Sher's criteria (≥50% AHI reduction and post-treatment AHI <20 events/h). RESULTS: Fifty patients had POSA and 32 had non-POSA. MAD therapy significantly improved total AHI, oxygen desaturation index, and oxygenation parameters in both groups. Treatment success occurred in 42/50 POSA patients (84.0%) and 30/32 non-POSA patients (93.8%; p = 0.332). Reductions in total AHI were also comparable between groups (19.19 ± 15.50 vs 24.14 ± 19.60 events/h; p = 0.232). Likewise, rates of achieving AHI <10 and <5 events/h did not differ significantly between groups. Positional phenotype was not significantly associated with treatment success. CONCLUSIONS: MAD therapy was associated with respiratory improvement regardless of positional phenotype. These findings do not support using POSA alone as a criterion for selecting candidates for MAD therapy. Larger prospective studies are required to confirm these results.

item.title: TM7x, an Ultrasmall Oral Episymbiont: Biology and Emerging Clinical Relevance.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrelou P, Alonaris E, Sergounioti A
item.description:
Authors: Dimitrelou P, Alonaris E, Sergounioti A
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70584
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43046504



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To review the biology of Nanosynbacter lyticus strain TM7x and critically assess its proposed relevance to periodontal disease. METHODS: This narrative review integrates foundational cultivation studies with a targeted PubMed update conducted on 29 October 2026. Human observational findings are distinguished from experimental evidence and from results concerning other Saccharibacteria. RESULTS: TM7x is an ultrasmall, genome-reduced episymbiont whose replication requires a compatible bacterial host. Studies of its interaction with Schaalia odontolytica XH001 reveal host adaptation, specialised pili, metabolic activity during transmission and changes in host physiology. Human disease associations frequently concern broader Saccharibacteria taxa and vary with population, sampling site and analytical method. Experimental studies demonstrate reduced inflammatory responses and, for several epibiont-host pairs, reduced bone loss in mice. These effects are context-dependent and do not establish clinical protection. Detailed knowledge of the species remains concentrated on the reference strain. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not establish TM7x as a causative human periodontal pathogen. It supports a model of context-dependent microbial and immune modulation, with unresolved consequences for human disease.

item.title: AI-Assisted Ni Classification in Nasopharyngeal NBI: Multicenter Validation and Reader Study.

item.description:
Authors: Huang JL, Li LJ, Wang ML, Zhu JQ, Dou LZ, Zhang X, Liu YM, Ke Y, Zhao YD, Wang JH, et al.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): To develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) system for standardized Ni classification of nasopharyngeal narrow-band imaging (NBI) and to evaluate whether AI assistance improves physician diagnostic consistency and biopsy-related decision making in a reader-study setting. METHODS: In this multicenter diagnostic study, 5404 high-quality nasopharyngeal NBI images were retrospectively collected. Lesion segmentation and five-class Ni classification networks were trained independently. Performance was evaluated in an internal test set, two independent external cohorts, and a recorded-video validation set. A prospective randomized multi-reader crossover study involving 12 physicians and 200 images from CHSZCAMS assessed the effect of AI assistance on diagnostic performance, inter-observer agreement, and potentially unnecessary biopsy decisions. RESULTS: In the two external cohorts, the model achieved accuracies of 0.889 and 0.873, with AUCs of 0.976 and 0.967, respectively. In recorded-video validation, accuracy was 0.888 and AUC was 0.974. CONCLUSION: AI-assisted Ni classification showed consistent diagnostic performance across validation cohorts and improved physician agreement across experience levels. item.title: Mitomycin C/5-Fluorouracil Versus Cisplatin/5-Fluorouracil With Hyperfractionated Accelerated Radiotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer: The ARO 04-01/AHMO Trial.

Published: 2026-Nov-17

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is the standard for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). For cisplatin (CDDP)-ineligible patients, mitomycin C/5-fluorouracil (MMC/5-FU) is the most common alternative, but randomized comparisons are lacking. We compared MMC/5-FU with CDDP/5-FU as concurrent partners of hyperfractionated-accelerated radiotherapy (HART) in unresectable, locally advanced HNSCC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this multicenter phase III trial, 364 patients with stage IVA/IVB (UICC TNM 6th edition) oropharyngeal or hypopharyngeal HNSCC were randomized 1:1 to HART (72 Gy/6 weeks) plus either weekly CDDP 30 mg/m² (n=182) or MMC 10 mg/m² on days 5 and 36 (n=182), both with continuous-infusion 5-FU 600 mg/m²/d on days 1-5. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS); secondary endpoints included freedom from progression (FFP), freedom from distant metastasis (FFDM), local, regional and locoregional control, and toxicity, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and, post hoc, in a competing-risk framework. RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 87 months, CDDP/5-FU was not superior for OS (10-year OS 23% vs. 18%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.89, 95% CI 0.69-1.15; log-rank p=0.418). In the competing-risk analysis, CDDP/5-FU reduced distant metastasis (5-year cumulative incidence 25.9% vs. 36.1%; subdistribution HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.45-0.96; p=0.031) and progression (45.6% vs. 56.3%; subdistribution HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.55-0.98; p=0.037). Kaplan-Meier estimates were directionally consistent but not significant (10-year FFDM 66% vs. 52%; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-1.02; p=0.060; FFP HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.59-1.05); local, regional and locoregional control (HR 0.80-1.01) and toxicity profiles did not differ. Serum creatinine (p<0.001) and the AE/SAE rate (24.2% vs. 15.4%; p=0.048) were higher with CDDP. CONCLUSION: ARO 04-01/AHMO did not show superiority of CDDP/5-FU over MMC/5-FU for overall survival. CDDP-based CRT remains the established standard for fit patients; MMC/5-FU is a safe and effective alternative with comparable overall survival and measurably lower nephrotoxicity and cumulative AE/SAE burden for CDDP-contraindicated patients. Abstract:
PURPOSE/OBJECTIVES: MnTnBuOE-2-PyP5+ (BMX-001) is a manganese metalloporphyrin superoxide dismutase mimic that inhibits radiation stress-induced pathways and may mitigate treatment-related side effects. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of BMX-001 on severe oral mucositis (OM), xerostomia, dermatitis, quality of life, and patient reported outcomes (PROs) among patients undergoing chemoradiation for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). MATERIALS/METHODS: This multicenter, phase I/II trial included patients with stage III-IVB HNSCC (AJCC 7th ed) undergoing definitive or postoperative chemoradiation (CRT). Patients received a subcutaneous BMX-001 loading dose followed by twice-weekly maintenance dosing through one week post-CRT at three loading/maintenance dose levels (7/3.5 mg, 14/7 mg, and 28/14 mg), with level 3 expanded for phase II endpoints. OM, xerostomia, and dermatitis were assessed weekly during treatment, within one month, and at six and 12 months post-chemoradiation. PROs and saliva production (stimulated and unstimulated) were measured at baseline, end of CRT, and one, six and 12 months post-CRT. Descriptive statistics summarized adverse events, symptom duration, and PROs. RESULTS: Between 5/2017 and 12/2019, 29 patients were enrolled; 86% had oropharynx primaries (n=25; n=24 HPV+) and 89.7% (n=26) underwent definitive CRT. One patient experienced two serious adverse events possibly related to BMX-001. Grade 3 OM occurred in 41.4% (n=12); acute and chronic grade ≥2 xerostomia occurred in 17.9% (n=5) and 9.1% (n=2), respectively, and 6.9% (n=2) experienced grade 3 dermatitis. At a median follow-up of 24 months, 96.6% were alive without progression. In exploratory longitudinal analyses of the 23 patients treated at the recommended phase II dose, patient-reported symptom and quality-of-life measures generally worsened at the end of CRT and subsequently improved. Several measures were no longer statistically different from baseline by six months, while measures of xerostomia remained elevated. CONCLUSIONS: BMX-001 is safe and feasible in patients with advanced HNSCC. In addition, BMX-001 shows promising efficacy for mitigating CRT-associated toxicity and warrants further study in larger, controlled trials.

item.title: Neoadjuvant talazoparib, irinotecan, and standard chemotherapy for early breast cancer in the I-SPY2 trial.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preclinical evidence suggests synergy between poly-ADP-ribose inhibitors and camptothecin chemotherapy. We tested the talazoparib and irinotecan combination (TI) in the neoadjuvant setting in the I-SPY2 trial in patients with HER2-negative locally advanced breast cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS: I-SPY2 is a phase II platform trial for stage 2/3 early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence. Participants were adaptively randomized to one of several experimental neoadjuvant therapies or control based on receptor subtypes defined by hormone receptor (HR), HER2 status, and MammaPrint risk (MP1, MP2). The primary endpoint was pathological complete response (pCR). Treatments 'graduate' if/when they achieve an 85% Bayesian probability of success in a subtype-specific phase III trial. Only HER2-negative patients were eligible for randomization to the TI arm. All patients received weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks, followed by doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide and surgery. Participants randomized to the TI arm received daily oral talazoparib and irinotecan infusions every other week. Pathway-specific biomarkers were assessed for response prediction. RESULTS: The combination of talazoparib and irinotecan failed to graduate from the I-SPY2 trial, with a 19% modeled posterior probability of pCR in the TI arm compared with 20% in the control arm among all patients with HER2-negative breast cancer. item.title: Prevalence and associated factors of influenza A virus infection among patients with acute respiratory tract infections in Gondar City, Northwest Ethiopia.

item.description:

Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0357953
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43043898



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Influenza A virus is a major cause of acute respiratory tract infections and contributes substantially to the global disease burden. Laboratory-confirmed data on influenza A virus infection remain limited in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of influenza A virus infection and to identify possible associated factors among patients with acute respiratory tract infections attending selected health institutions in Gondar City, Northwest Ethiopia. METHODS: A multi-center, health facility-based cross-sectional study was carried out from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025. In total, 490 patients with acute respiratory tract infections were enrolled from five health facilities in Gondar City. Demographic, behavioral, and clinical information was collected using a structured questionnaire. Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected and tested for influenza A virus using multiplex real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with influenza A virus infection. RESULTS: Influenza A virus was detected in 65 of the 490 participants, with an overall prevalence of 13.3% (95% CI: 10.3-16.3). Among the confirmed cases, 48 (73.8%) were A(H1N1) and 17 (26.2%) were A(H3N2). In multivariable logistic regression, participants aged 5-17 years (AOR: 3.14; 95% CI: 1.36-7.25; p = 0.008) and 18-49 years (AOR: 3.50; 95% CI: 1.54-7.20; p = 0.002) had higher odds of infection than those aged <5 years. Secondary education was associated with lower odds of infection compared with no formal education (AOR: 0.07; 95% CI: 0.01-0.75; p = 0.029), while employed participants had higher odds than students (AOR: 3.54; 95% CI: 1.47-7.80; p = 0.028). CONCLUSION: Influenza A virus infection was detected among patients presenting with acute respiratory tract infections in Gondar City, highlighting the importance of influenza surveillance and laboratory confirmation in this population. Strengthening routine molecular surveillance, promoting seasonal influenza vaccination among high-risk populations, reinforcing infection prevention and control measures, and implementing targeted community health education are essential to improve influenza prevention and control.

item.title: Age as a determinant of trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries in pediatric emergency department visits: A NEISS analysis.
item.dc:creator: Wiener RC, Waters C
item.description:
Authors: Wiener RC, Waters C
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362482
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43043884



Abstract:
Over the last decade trampoline use has increased. Many injuries occur that require emergency department (ED) care. The purpose of this research is to examine the role of age in trampoline-related oral-facial-head injuries that require ED care. Data from the 2024 National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) was used. Trampoline-related injuries were extracted from the data set. Oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries were compared with other types of trampoline-related injuries by age groups (0 to <6 years, 6 to <12 years, and 12 to ≤18 years) in Chi-Square analyses and logistic regression analyses. There were 3548 NEISS-reported trampoline-associated injuries for children, ages 0 to ≤18 years, in 2024. This corresponded to an estimated 101,474 trampoline injuries in the United States in 2024. Of these, 21.7% were oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries (weighted estimate of 22,033 injuries). Of all the trampoline-related injuries in children ages 0 to ≤18 years, children ages 0 to <6 years had 33.0% of the injuries; children ages 6 to <12 years had 51.9%; and, children ages 12 to ≤18 years had 15.1%. Children ages 0 to <6 years had an adjusted odds ratio of 1.66 [95% CI: 1.11, 2.50; p = 0.0155] compared with children ages 12 to ≤18 years for oral-facial-head trampoline-related injuries as compared with other injuries from trampolines. These findings highlight the need for targeted prevention and anticipatory guidance for younger children.

item.title: ERBB2 amplification and salivary-gland-enriched residual non-ICI scenario-based genomic signal coverage in head and neck cancer comprehensive genomic profiling: a nationwide C-CAT analysis.

Authors: Kajiura S, Nakamura N, Hayashi R
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10829-1

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) in head and neck cancer can return tumor-agnostic and histology-associated signals, but practical benchmarks for reported ERBB2 amplification and residual non-immune-checkpoint-inhibitor (non-ICI) scenario-based genomic signal coverage are limited. We quantified the contribution of ERBB2 amplification and ALK fusion/rearrangement in nationwide Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics (C-CAT) data, focusing on salivary gland tumors and salivary duct carcinoma. METHODS: This retrospective descriptive scenario-based analysis included anonymized C-CAT-derived head and neck CGP-tested cases. Overall and residual non-ICI frameworks were assessed before ERBB2, after adding reported ERBB2 amplification, and after adding ALK fusion/rearrangement as an updated 2026 layer. RESULTS: The cohort included 3,089 cases. In the overall framework, scenario-based genomic signal coverage increased from 280/3,089 (9.1%) to 501/3,089 (16.2%) after adding reported ERBB2 amplification (+ 221 cases; +7.2% points). In the residual non-ICI framework, the increase was from 61/3,089 (2.0%) to 309/3,089 (10.0%) (+ 248 cases; +8.0% points). Reported ERBB2 amplification was detected in 249/3,089 (8.1%), and the descriptive ERBB2 union in 379/3,089 (12.3%). In salivary duct carcinoma, reported ERBB2 amplification occurred in 105/262 (40.1%), the descriptive ERBB2 union in 124/262 (47.3%), and residual non-ICI post-ERBB2 framework positivity in 114/262 (43.5%). ALK fusion/rearrangement added 0 cases. CONCLUSION: Reported ERBB2 amplification materially increased scenario-based genomic signal coverage in head and neck cancer, especially salivary duct carcinoma. These findings provide an implementation-level benchmark for CGP counseling and expert-panel discussion in head and neck oncology.

item.title: Molecular Residual Disease After Definitive Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer: Clinical Value and Optimal Timing for ctDNA Assessment.
item.dc:creator: Bruixola G, Martín-Arana J, Gimeno-Valiente F, Villarroel-Espindola F, Alfaro-Cervelló C, Dualde D, Grimalt N, García Bartolomé M, García-Márquez A, Iglesias-Martinez B, et al.

Journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research | DOI: 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-26-1545

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate post-treatment assessment after definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC) remains challenging due to limitations of standard imaging. We evaluated the diagnostic performance, prognostic value and optimal timing of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for molecular residual disease (MRD) detection. METHODS: Seventy-four patients with LA-HNSCC treated with definitive CRT were prospectively enrolled. Plasma samples were collected before treatment, at 8 and 12 weeks after CRT, and during follow-up. ctDNA was analysed using a plasma-only methylation-based assay. Diagnostic performance for recurrence detection and associations with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated and compared with 12-week PET/CT findings. RESULTS: Baseline ctDNA was detectable in 85.1% of patients. Among post-treatment timepoints, week-12 ctDNA showed the highest diagnostic accuracy for recurrence detection, with 69% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% positive predictive value, and 76% negative predictive value. Detectable week-12 ctDNA was associated with shorter PFS (HR, 6.44; 95% CI, 2.73-16.74; p<0.001) and OS (HR, 7.31; 95% CI, 2.80-22.31; p<0.001 ). CONCLUSIONS: Plasma-only methylation-based ctDNA provided high-specificity prognostic information after definitive CRT in LA-HNSCC, particularly at week 12 and in PET partial-responders. ctDNA may complement PET/CT for post-treatment risk stratification, but should not be used as a stand-alone test to exclude recurrence.

item.title: Positive Surgical Margins in Sinonasal Cancer: A Contemporary Analysis of Risk Factors and Survival.
item.dc:creator: Fu BJ, Moon P, Lee JJ, Ayoub NF

Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71066
Published: 2026-Nov-16

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal cancers (SNCs) are rare, aggressive malignancies in which surgery remains a cornerstone of multimodal treatment. Contemporary national data on positive surgical margins (PSM), risk factors, and survival implications are limited. We evaluated temporal trends, predictors, and prognostic significance of PSMs in SNC. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the National Cancer Database (2015-2022). Adults with cT1-4bN0M0 SNC undergoing definitive surgery were included; those with unknown tumor size, prior malignancy, or missing margin status were excluded. PSM trends were assessed using the Cuzick test and logistic regression; risk factors using generalized linear models; and overall survival using Kaplan-Meier, multivariable Cox proportional hazards, and 1:1 propensity score-matched analyses. RESULTS: The final cohort included 753 patients (mean age 63.4 years [SD 11.8]; 33.2% female). PSMs occurred in 253 patients (33.6%), increasing from 29.6% in 2015 to 41.8% in 2022 (adjusted OR 1.09/year, 95% CI 1.02-1.17). Independent predictors included cT3-T4b stage (aRR 1.53, 95% CI 1.09-2.13), maxillary sinus origin (aRR 1.54, 95% CI 1.22-1.96), Charlson-Deyo score ≥ 3 (aRR 1.42, 95% CI 1.01-1.99), conversion to open surgery (aRR 2.01, 95% CI 1.14-3.55), and Native American race (aRR 2.92, 95% CI 1.65-5.18). PSMs independently predicted worse survival in multivariable (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.27-2.19) and propensity score-matched analyses (aHR 2.13, 95% CI 1.39-3.26). CONCLUSIONS: PSMs remain common in SNC, increasing over time and independently predicting worse survival. Efforts to refine surgical techniques and multidisciplinary, histology-guided treatment strategies may improve oncologic outcomes.

item.title: EUSICA/INSICA Position Paper on Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Nasal Vestibule: A Distinct Clinical Entity Requiring Dedicated Classification, Treatment Strategies and Outcome Measures.

item.description:
Authors: de Ridder M, Breimer G, Bossi P, von Buchwald C, Bussu F, Capper D, Choby G, Devriese LA, Ferrand FR, Gallia GL, et al.

Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43039669



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Cancer of the nasal vestibule (CNV) differs anatomically and clinically from both sinonasal and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, yet lacks formal recognition as a separate clinical entity and topographical subsite; whether it is also biologically distinct has not yet been investigated. EUSICA/INSICA advocates for formal recognition of CNV and a unified classification, treatment, and translational framework. METHOD: Published literature on CNV, including population-based cohorts, T-classification studies, brachytherapy outcomes, and quality-of-life data, was reviewed by an international multidisciplinary EUSICA/INSICA expert panel to formulate consensus recommendations. FINDING: CNV shows favorable outcomes, drains preferentially to facial and submandibular nodes, and is amenable to organ-preserving radiotherapy, in particular brachytherapy. It is staged using four non-uniform systems; multicenter validation in 609 patients from 21 centers supported the prognostic utility of the New Rome classification integrated with clinical nodal status. Validated CNV-specific quality-of-life instruments are lacking. Compared with NCCN-defined high-risk cutaneous SCC of the nose, CNV differs in topography, pattern of local spread, prognostic landmarks, nodal behavior, and treatment paradigm. Comparative molecular data versus cutaneous and sinonasal SCC are not yet available. CONCLUSION: EUSICA/INSICA calls for formal recognition of CNV as a distinct ICD-O-3 subsite, incorporation of the New Rome T classification into UICC/AJCC TNM, standardized organ-preserving treatment, and dedicated translational research, including comparative molecular studies to determine whether its clinical distinctness has a biological basis.

item.title: Exploring the Financial Toxicity and Opportunity Costs of Smoking in Lung and Head and Neck Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Stemme RA, Najjar W, Armache M, Lababidi G, Samaha NL, Kacker S, Gentsch AT, Gharzai LA, Galiatsatos P, St John MA, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Stemme RA, Najjar W, Armache M, Lababidi G, Samaha NL, Kacker S, Gentsch AT, Gharzai LA, Galiatsatos P, St John MA, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71065
Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43039448



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with lung and head and neck cancers (L/HNC) face disproportionately high rates of financial toxicity (FT) and persistent smoking after diagnosis, yet the relationship between tobacco use, associated spending, and FT remains poorly understood. This study characterizes this relationship in patients with L/HNC. METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods study with semi-structured interviews from 03/2024 to 03/2025 and data analyzed from 07/2024 to 11/2025. Patients with newly diagnosed L/HNC were enrolled through convenience sampling. Transcripts were analyzed using content analysis until thematic saturation. Participants completed the Comprehensive Score for Financial Toxicity (COST) (11-items; 0-44, lower scores represent worse FT), USDA Six-Item Short Form Food Security Module, and smoking-induced deprivation (SID) questionnaire to assess psychosocial, material, and behavioral FT components, respectively. RESULTS: Among 25 participants (13 [52%]) male; 18 (72%) non-Hispanic White; median age 61 years (range, 44-78 years)], 12 (48%) were current smokers at diagnosis. Median COST score was 21 (range 4-43), with 15 (63%) experiencing FT (COST < 26). Eight (33%) patients reported food insecurity. Participants spent a median of $155 (IQR $63-$285) monthly on cigarettes, and 4 (17%) reported SID. Qualitative analysis confirmed an established FT framework and identified tobacco use and spending as a bidirectional contributor to FT. CONCLUSIONS: Tobacco use and spending have a bidirectional relationship with FT, contributing to FT across the material, psychosocial, and behavioral domains, while serving as a coping mechanism for financial distress. Our findings underscore the need for integrated smoking cessation and FT interventions alongside targeted FT screening for patients with a smoking history.

item.title: Clinical characteristics and oncologic outcomes of young adults with squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue: A multicenter retrospective study.
item.dc:creator: Gazzini L, Liberale C, Guerra G, Querzoli G, Ferrari M, Ruaro A, Pangallo S, Montenegro C, Molendi C, Belponer G, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Gazzini L, Liberale C, Guerra G, Querzoli G, Ferrari M, Ruaro A, Pangallo S, Montenegro C, Molendi C, Belponer G, et al.
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108195
Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43038652



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic significance of young age in squamous cell carcinoma of the mobile tongue and floor of mouth remains controversial. We compared clinicopathological characteristics and oncologic outcomes between young and older patients undergoing surgery. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included patients treated with primary curative-intent surgery at 13 high-volume European cancer centers between 2012 and 2022. Patients were stratified as young (≤40 years) or older (≥55 years); those aged 41-54 years were excluded. Clinicopathological variables, recurrence, overall survival (OS), and disease-specific survival (DSS) were compared. RESULTS: Among 375 patients, 133 were young and 242 older. Younger patients were more often never smokers (67.2% vs 47.5%; p = 0.001), non-drinkers (95.1% vs 74.5%; p < 0.001), and had early pT disease (62.9% vs 48.3%; p = 0.009) and lower tumor grade (p = 0.041). Pathological nodal involvement, lymphovascular invasion, perineural invasion, and extranodal extension were comparable. Younger patients had higher odds of positive margins (18.3% vs 10.5%; OR 1.898; p = 0.034). In advanced pT disease, perineural invasion was more frequent in younger patients (71.4% vs 54.5%; p = 0.042). OS, DSS, and recurrence did not differ significantly between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Young adults show lower tobacco and alcohol exposure and more favorable local tumor features without improved oncologic outcomes. Young age should not be considered an inherently favorable prognostic factor. Further translational studies are warranted to clarify the biological mechanisms underlying early-onset disease.

item.title: Struggling minds in lower ranks: Stronger ACC-OFC-amygdala coupling despite reduced selection of effortful options in subordinate male rats.
item.dc:creator: Roshani G, Heysieattalab S, Farkhondeh Tale Navi F
item.description:
Authors: Roshani G, Heysieattalab S, Farkhondeh Tale Navi F
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362370
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43038302



Abstract:
Social hierarchy can influence how individuals allocate effort to obtain rewards, but the neural mechanisms underlying rank-related differences in effort-based decision-making remain unclear. We investigated whether social rank is associated with effort-based choice and local and interregional neural activity in male rats. Twenty-one male Wistar rats were classified as dominant, intermediate, or subordinate based on repeated tube-test performance. Rats then performed a T-maze effort-based decision-making task in which they chose between a high-reward/high-effort option (six food pellets with a 30-cm barrier) and a low-reward/no-effort option (two food pellets without a barrier). Local field potentials were recorded from the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), and amygdala (AM). Dominant rats selected the high-reward/high-effort option more frequently than intermediate and subordinate rats, whereas response latency did not differ significantly among social-rank groups. Subordinate rats exhibited greater theta and high-gamma power in the ACC, OFC, and AM, as well as greater low-beta power in selected regions. Interregional coherence differed across social-rank groups in a frequency- and pathway-specific manner. Subordinate rats generally showed greater low-beta and high-gamma coherence in the OFC-AM, OFC-ACC, and ACC-AM pathways, whereas dominant rats showed greater theta coherence in the OFC-ACC and ACC-AM pathways. Several associations between neural measures and choice behavior were observed, particularly for low-beta and high-gamma activity and coherence, although these relationships varied across social-rank groups and neural pathways. These findings indicate that social rank is associated with differences in effort-based choice and with frequency- and pathway-specific alterations in ACC-OFC-AM neural dynamics. Overall, the findings suggest that social experience and hierarchical position are associated with distinct patterns of cortical-limbic activity during effort-based decision-making.

item.title: Impact of nicotine concentration, form, and stereoisomer ratio on oral nicotine pouch pharmacokinetics and abuse liability: Protocol for a randomized crossover study in adults who use tobacco.
item.dc:creator: Tomko PM, Cho YJ, Curran H, Hinton A, Wagener TL, Brinkman MC, Keller-Hamilton B
item.description:
Authors: Tomko PM, Cho YJ, Curran H, Hinton A, Wagener TL, Brinkman MC, Keller-Hamilton B
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362198
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43038220



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Oral nicotine pouches (ONPs) are tobacco-free products placed between the lip and gum to deliver nicotine. Sales have grown rapidly in the United States (U.S.), yet independent data on how nicotine characteristics shape ONP appeal and addiction potential are lacking. Three nicotine characteristics vary across ONPs: concentration (mass of nicotine per pouch), form (the fraction of freebase, or unprotonated, nicotine), and stereoisomer (the proportion of S- to R-nicotine). This study will determine how these characteristics independently and jointly affect ONP nicotine pharmacokinetics and user experience among adults who smoke cigarettes or use moist snuff. DESIGN AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized, double-blind, crossover trial will enroll 160 adults who smoke cigarettes or use moist snuff at a single U.S. site. INTERVENTIONS AND OUTCOMES: Participants will be randomized 1:1 to a lower (3 mg) or higher (6 mg) nicotine concentration arm. Within each arm, participants will complete five laboratory sessions in balanced, randomized order: four standardized ONP sessions (30 minutes, with the pouch placed between lip and gum) varying by nicotine form (30% vs. 70% freebase) and stereoisomer ratio (racemic [50% R- and 50% S-nicotine] vs. > 99% S-nicotine), plus one session using their usual tobacco product. Sessions will be separated by at least 48 hours. The primary outcome is maximum plasma nicotine concentration (Cmax). Secondary outcomes include time to maximum concentration (Tmax), total nicotine absorbed over 90 minutes (AUC), subjective effects, and behavioral economic demand indices. CONCLUSIONS: This will be the first study to systematically examine how nicotine concentration, form, and stereoisomer ratio interact to influence ONP abuse liability. Findings will identify which product characteristics drive ONP addiction potential and will inform FDA regulation aimed at maximizing the potential for ONPs to serve as a harm reduction alternative to cigarettes and moist snuff. item.title: Innovative mHealth intervention providing sustained anticipatory guidance (zero cavity): Design, validation, user perception and effectiveness - A randomized controlled trial protocol.
item.dc:creator: Murugan SM, Dhar V, Saikia A, Sampath V, Ramendran H, Balakrishnan K, Nirmal L, Pasupathy U, Davis J
item.description:
Authors: Murugan SM, Dhar V, Saikia A, Sampath V, Ramendran H, Balakrishnan K, Nirmal L, Pasupathy U, Davis J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0359152
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43038214



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early Childhood Caries (ECC) remains one of the most common chronic conditions in childhood, affecting over 600 million children globally. When untreated, it can lead to severe pain, abscesses, difficulty in chewing that contributes to malnutrition, impaired speech, disrupted sleep, low self-esteem, social withdrawal, and poor academic performance, all of which diminish a child's overall quality of life. Although largely preventable, ECC remains highly prevalent because of delayed preventive care and low parental awareness. Effective health education needs to be consistent, accessible, and available whenever parents need it. Although current evidence indicates that anticipatory guidance is a proven approach, its long-term reinforcement through a mobile app has not yet been tested. This study aims to develop and evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile health (mHealth) application delivering Sustained Anticipatory Guidance (SAG) for the prevention of ECC. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: A two-arm parallel hospital-based randomized controlled trial will be conducted at Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education & Research, Chennai, India. The study will enrol 540 mother-infant dyads from the departments of Pediatric Medicine and the Centre for Early Childhood Caries Research (CECCRe). Eligible dyads with infants aged 6-12 months in the predentate stage will be randomized to the "Zero-Cavity" mHealth app (intervention) or standard care (control). Baseline and semi-annual data on oral hygiene, fluoride exposure, and feeding/diet will be collected. Calibrated dentists will perform quarterly clinical exams using ICDAS II criteria, recording cavitated and non-cavitated lesions. For children at high risk or with enamel defects/incipient lesions, clinical photographs will be taken to support individualized preventive guidance. The primary outcome will be the effectiveness of the app in preventing ECC, while the secondary outcomes will include ECC incidence and prevalence. DISCUSSION: Despite being largely preventable, ECC remains a major public health challenge, sustained by limited preventive access and inconsistent counselling, especially in LMICs. This trial evaluates the Zero Cavity app, believed to bridge this gap by providing sustained, age-appropriate anticipatory guidance beyond clinic settings on oral development, hygiene, diet/feeding, and fluoride use. The behavioural theory-driven approach is expected to enhance cultural relevance, usability, and behaviour change, with optimism that process evaluation will illuminate engagement and implementation. It is believed that this large, adequately powered, parallel-group RCT with intention-to-treat analysis will offer, with optimism, a scalable, low-cost model that will expand the reach and consistency of continuous preventive care in diverse urban and peri-urban populations. item.title: Downregulation of miR-548c-3p potentially drives IL-17 pathway dysregulation in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Nasim MT, Rana NA, Mukhtar U, Sheryar M, Rabia G, Sehar S, Khan MJ, Khan MJ, Awan HM
item.description:
Authors: Nasim MT, Rana NA, Mukhtar U, Sheryar M, Rabia G, Sehar S, Khan MJ, Khan MJ, Awan HM
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362467
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43038194



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: MicroRNAs fine-tune gene expression and control signaling pathways. When perturbed, they can have serious consequences, such as cancer. Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most prevalent form of oral-related malignancies. Among different signaling pathways, the IL-17 pathway is strongly associated with the aggressive course of OSCC. We investigated the expression of a primate-specific miR-548c-3p and its potential association with IL-17 pathway-related genes. AIMS: Study the expression of hsa-miR-548c-3p and its target genes of IL-17 pathway in oral cancer. METHODOLOGY: Bioinformatics analysis was conducted on OSCC microarray datasets to identify dysregulated genes. KEGG pathway analysis was used to identify IL-17 pathway genes. Experimental validation was conducted using RT-qPCR, correlation between miRNA and its putative target genes was conducted using Spearman correlation, and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using ROC analysis. RESULTS: Among the 379 predicted targets of miR-548c-3p, FOSL1 and SRSF1, key genes in the IL-17 pathway, exhibited significant up-regulation in the bioinformatic analysis. Experimental validation confirmed the significant down-regulation of miR-548c-3p alongside a significant up-regulation of SRSF1, where correlation analysis revealed a strong inverse relation between them, whereas FOSL1 showed a non-significant up-regulation and a moderate inverse association with miR-548c-3p. ROC analysis demonstrated strong diagnostic potential for both miR-548c-3p and SRSF1. CONCLUSION: hsa-miR-548c-3p down-regulation is inversely correlated with both IL-17 pathway genes, ROC curve analysis underscores the potential diagnostic biomarker potential of hsa-miR-548c-3p and SRSF1, establishing them as promising therapeutic targets in OSCC.

item.title: Recurrence in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: a retrospective surgical cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Clari-Comes M, Martin-Jimenez D, Moreno-Luna R, Gonzalez-Garcia J, Gonzalez-Garcia M, Vizcarra-Melgar J, Lekue-Madinabeitia A, Sanchez-Gomez S

Authors: Clari-Comes M, Martin-Jimenez D, Moreno-Luna R, Gonzalez-Garcia J, Gonzalez-Garcia M, Vizcarra-Melgar J, Lekue-Madinabeitia A, Sanchez-Gomez S

Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43037710



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the association of endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) strategy with the frequency and timing of postoperative recurrence in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), using prespecified clinical-endoscopic criteria. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study with 3-year follow-up was conducted in CRSwNP patients who underwent ESS. Surgical procedures were classified according to the Lamella Ostium Extent Mucosa (LOEM) system (t1-t4). Postoperative recurrence was defined by symptom worsening and/or endoscopic evidence of polyp relapse. Logistic regression identified independent predictors of recurrence, while Kaplan-Meier and Cox models assessed recurrence-free survival. A Cox-derived prognostic index, based on the model linear predictor, was used to stratify patients into risk groups. RESULTS: In the overall sample (n = 172), 38.4% of patients met recurrence criteria, with rates varying across LOEM groups. Extensive ESS (t3-t4) was associated with significantly lower recurrence risk (OR = 0.10 and 0.28) and longer recurrence-free survival (HR = 0.51, p = 0.038). Exploratory subgroup Cox analyses identified nominally significant associations with lower recurrence hazards in patients with asthma (HR = 0.21), N-ERD (HR = 0.28), atopy (HR = 0.25) and total IgE > 100 (HR = 0.22), with similar patterns in women, surgery-naive and delayed-ESS cases. Prognostic stratification showed a clear gradient in recurrence burden from 12.1% to 58.6% across risk groups, with higher-risk strata displaying a progressively more unfavorable type 2 inflammatory profile and greater baseline disease burden. CONCLUSION: Surgical extent was associated with both recurrence risk and timing. Extensive ESS (t3-t4) was associated with more sustained disease control, with exploratory signals in selected type 2-associated profiles. These findings support further investigation of individualized surgical strategies, although further studies are needed.

item.title: Hypoactive APOBEC3A Achieves High-Level Mutagenesis and Drives Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

item.description:
Authors: Xu Z, Flensburg C, O'Reilly LA, Bilardi RA, Whitehead LW, Chen DK, Kueh A, Sutherland KD, Majewski IJ
Journal: Cancer research | DOI: 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-25-5211
Published: 2026-Nov-16

Abstract:
APOBEC proteins shape the somatic mutation spectrum of many cancers by binding and editing DNA. Modeling APOBEC-induced changes in cancer has been challenging due to the toxicity of these enzymes. Here, we overcame this barrier using a mutant form of APOBEC3A with impaired deaminase activity by changing arginine 128 to alanine (A3AR128A). Overexpressing A3AR128A in murine epithelium induced squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) in the skin, head and neck region, and cervix, mirroring the human disease spectrum. Tumor formation was further accelerated by concomitant Trp53 loss. A3AR128A cancers carried frequent alterations in the NOTCH and RAS-PI3K pathways, and recurrent mutations in genes encoding histone H3 were also observed. Cross-species analysis revealed how APOBEC accessibility influences cancer driver gene selection. A catalogue of 235,790 mutations was used to refine mutational signatures linked to A3A. These results shed light on how DNA damage from A3A contributes to tumorigenesis.

item.title: Optimizing Induction Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Risk-Stratified Recursive Partitioning Analysis Based on 9th Edition Staging.
item.dc:creator: Lin J, Wang T, Xiao J, Lin J, Liu T, Lu J, Mo H, Xie R, Mai H, Chen Q
item.description:
Authors: Lin J, Wang T, Xiao J, Lin J, Liu T, Lu J, Mo H, Xie R, Mai H, Chen Q
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70819
Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43037240



Abstract:
Although induction chemotherapy (IC) in combination with concurrent chemoradiotherapy constitutes the standard treatment for locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LANPC), the optimal number of IC cycles remains undetermined. The 9th edition staging system provides a refined risk stratification framework. We aimed to develop a prognostic tool to stratify patients with LANPC and define the optimal number of IC cycles for distinct risk groups based on new staging. We analyzed 1216 patients with LANPC treated with IC and employed propensity score matching to minimize bias. Progression-free survival (PFS) was the primary endpoint, analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves. A recursive partitioning analysis (RPA) model was developed and validated for risk stratification. Survival outcomes and toxicities were compared across IC cycle groups. After a median follow-up of 56 months, 2- and 3-cycle IC yielded greater improvements in PFS compared with 4-cycle IC (p < 0.001). The RPA model incorporated 9th edition staging, pretreatment EBV DNA, and IC response, stratifying patients into three risk categories. For low-risk patients, 2- and 3-cycle IC yielded comparable PFS, both superior to 4-cycle IC (p < 0.001). In intermediate-risk patients, significantly higher 5-year PFS was achieved with 2-cycle IC than with 3- (73.4% vs. 56.2%, p = 0.014) or 4-cycle IC (73.4% vs. 47.5%, p < 0.001). High-risk patients benefited more from 3-cycle versus 2- (47.5% vs. 31.7%; p = 0.038) or 4-cycle IC (47.5% vs. 36.2%; p = 0.039). Overall, the RPA-based model effectively stratified risk, guiding individualized IC cycle selection. Balancing toxicity and efficacy, 2-cycle IC is optimal for the low- and intermediate-risk groups, while 3-cycle IC is preferred for the high-risk group.

item.title: Prognostic Predictors in Patients With Necrotizing Otitis Externa: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.dc:creator: Kim S, Na HS, Lee S, Kim SH, Lee HM, Oh SJ, Lee IW, Hwangbo L, Choi SW
item.description:
Authors: Kim S, Na HS, Lee S, Kim SH, Lee HM, Oh SJ, Lee IW, Hwangbo L, Choi SW
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70525
Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43036977



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Necrotizing otitis externa (NOE) is a rare infection with a heterogeneous clinical course that complicates prognostication. The impact of diabetes mellitus on outcomes remains controversial, and objective predictors of treatment duration are unclear. This study aimed to identify the factors associated with prolonged hospitalization in patients with NOE. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational study. SETTING: Tertiary academic medical center. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 61 patients with NOE admitted between September 2009 and October 2024. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, microbiological, and radiological data, as well as length of hospital stay, were analyzed. Magnetic resonance imaging assessed skull-base osteomyelitis and white matter lesions using the Fazekas scale. Multivariable linear regression identified factors associated with hospital stay. RESULTS: The mean age was 70.25 ± 13.11 years (63.9% male; mean hospital stay 46.02 ± 37.50 days). Diabetes was present in 75.4% of the patients, but neither diabetes nor hemoglobin A1c levels were associated with hospital stay. In the univariate analysis, diabetic complications, external auditory canal swelling, cranial nerve palsy, peak inflammatory marker levels, inflammatory marker normalization times, and higher Fazekas scores were associated with prolonged hospitalization, whereas only diabetic complications and higher Fazekas scores remained independently associated in the multivariable analysis (adjusted R2 = 0.425). CONCLUSION: Diabetic complications and higher Fazekas scores were independently associated with prolonged hospitalization in patients with NOE. These findings suggest that chronic microvascular disease burden, rather than conventional vascular risk factors alone, may contribute to a prolonged disease course. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings.

item.title: Evaluating the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index for Predicting Outcomes Following Head and Neck Free-Flap Reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Kaki PC, Goldfarb JA, Bridgham K, Curry J, Thal A
item.description:
Authors: Kaki PC, Goldfarb JA, Bridgham K, Curry J, Thal A
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70528
Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43036969



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Malnutrition has been associated with adverse outcomes among head and neck cancer (HNC) patients. Despite this, there is no universally accepted standard for screening of nutrition-related risk. This study aimed to determine if nutrition-related risk, as defined by the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI), is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes following microvascular free tissue transfer (MFTT) for HNC. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Population-based study using the 2010 to 2022 American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP). METHODS: Patients aged >65 years who underwent MFTT for HNC were stratified into 3 cohorts based on preoperative GNRI: no nutrition-related risk (GNRI > 98), moderate nutrition-related risk (GNRI 92-98), and major nutrition-related risk (GNRI < 92). After adjusting for potential confounders, multivariable logistic regression models were performed to assess the association between GNRI and postoperative outcomes. RESULTS: Of 1586 patients, 945 (59.6%) patients had a GNRI corresponding with no nutrition-related risk, 346 (21.8%) had moderate nutrition-related risk, and 295 (18.6%) had major nutrition-related risk. On multivariable regression, both moderate and major nutrition-related risk cohorts were associated with surgical, medical, and Clavien-Dindo grade IV (CDIV) complications, along with non-home discharge, respectively (P < .05). CONCLUSIONS: Nutrition-related risk as defined by the GNRI is associated with surgical, medical, and CDIV complications, and non-home discharge following MFTT for HNC. Prospective studies are needed to validate the utility of the GNRI as a preoperative risk stratification tool to optimize surgical outcomes following MFTT for HNC.

item.title: Global and Regional Epidemiology of Early-Onset Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma From 1990 to 2021.
item.dc:creator: Yu S, Shen L, Huang Y
item.description:
Authors: Yu S, Shen L, Huang Y
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70515
Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43036952



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined the global burden of early-onset nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). STUDY DESIGN: Data on early-onset NPC patients aged 15 to 49 years from 1990 to 2021 were from GBD 2021 to evaluate disease burden and forecast to 2050. SETTING: Early-onset NPC patients aged 15 to 49 years; Global Burden of Disease (GBD) database 2021; period 1990 to 2021. METHODS: The burden of NPC was evaluated using incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), sociodemographic index (SDI), and average annual percentage change (AAPC). Changes in risk factors affecting NPC were also analyzed. Bayesian age-period-cohort analysis was applied to forecast the disease burden spanning 2022 to 2050. RESULTS: Globally, the incidence, mortality, and DALYs of early-onset NPC all declined during 1990 to 2021. The AAPC of incidence, mortality, and DALYs were -0.32 (95% CI: -0.39 to -0.26), -2.12 (-2.16 to -2.08), and -2.09 (-2.13 to -2.05), respectively. The DALYs for NPC exhibited a markedly declining trend among various SDI regions over the 1990-2021 period. East Asia [AAPC: -3.19 (-3.26 to -3.12)] and Western Europe [AAPC: -3.04 (-3.16 to -2.96)] experienced the largest drops in DALYs from 1990 to 2021. High alcohol consumption, smoking, and formaldehyde exposure were major contributing factors to DALYs for early-onset NPC, with no significant changes observed between 1990 and 2021. From 2022 to 2050, the disease burden of early-onset NPC worldwide is projected to decline. CONCLUSIONS: Globally, the burden of early-onset NPC declined during 1990 to 2021 period and is projected to continue to decline in the future.

item.title: Fine motor impairment in long-term survivors of nasopharyngeal carcinoma after intensity-modulated radiotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Wong GC, Lui JCF, Lau AMC, Cheung KM, Au KH, Lau AYL, Zee BC, Chow JC
item.description:
Authors: Wong GC, Lui JCF, Lau AMC, Cheung KM, Au KH, Lau AYL, Zee BC, Chow JC
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108232
Published: 2026-Nov-15
PMID: 43038651



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Characterize fine motor outcomes among nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) survivors and associated clinical and radiation dose factors. METHODS: We enrolled 190 NPC survivors at a median of 7.0 years (range, 1.0-13.6) after definitive intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT); 86.3 % (164/190) received concurrent chemotherapy. Fine motor function was evaluated using Grooved Pegboard Test (GP) Z-scores normalized to age and educational level. Motor-related regions of interest (ROIs), including bilateral precentral and postcentral gyri, thalami, striata, cerebella, brain stem, and spinal cord, were segmented in 105 patients for dosimetric analyses. RESULTS: NPC survivors exhibited significant bilateral fine motor impairment compared with normative data (median GP Z-score, -0.3; p < 0.001); 22.1 % (42/190) and 18.9 % (36/190) of patients scored ≥ 2 standard deviations below norms for their dominant and nondominant hands respectively. Advanced T-category was associated with higher radiation doses to motor ROIs and poorer GP Z-scores in both dominant (p < 0.001) and nondominant hands (p = 0.014). Higher Dmax and D1 % to the precentral gyri were associated with poorer GP Z-scores in the corresponding hands. High cumulative cisplatin exposure was associated with worse motor performance in both hands (dominant, p < 0.001; nondominant, p = 0.028); patients who received 450-600 mg/m2 had GP Z-scores equivalent to 43 years of age-related motor dexterity decline compared with those receiving 0-<150 mg/m2. CONCLUSIONS: NPC survivors demonstrated substantial long-term fine motor impairment associated with T-category, radiation dose to the precentral gyri, and cumulative cisplatin exposure. These findings highlight the importance of personalized treatment to minimize neurotoxicity, and long-term fine motor monitoring and rehabilitation for NPC survivors.

item.title: Oral Cancer Screening in the Landscape of Randomized Controlled Trials: A Scoping Review.
item.dc:creator: Calderipe CB, Pedroso CM, Lopes MA, Warnakulasuriya S, Santos-Silva AR
item.description:
Authors: Calderipe CB, Pedroso CM, Lopes MA, Warnakulasuriya S, Santos-Silva AR
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70573
Published: 2026-Nov-15
PMID: 43036236



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify the types of cancer and the corresponding screening methods evaluated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs), with a primary focus on situating oral cancer screening within the RCT-based body of evidence. METHODS: This review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, LILACS, ProQuest, and Google Scholar were searched without date restrictions for studies in English, Spanish, or Portuguese. Eligible studies were RCTs primarily evaluating cancer screening methods (clinical, imaging, endoscopic, laboratory, molecular/serological, or self-examination). Data were synthesized as means and frequencies. RESULTS: Nine cancer types and 33 distinct screening methods were identified across 97 cancer screenings in 91 RCTs spanning 57 years. Oral cancer ranked last, with only one RCT evaluating a single method, oral visual inspection, the fewest of any cancer type. By comparison, colorectal cancer was the most frequently investigated (n = 22/22.7%), followed by breast cancer (n = 21/21.6%) and lung cancer (n = 18/18.6%), with five, six, and four screening methods evaluated, respectively. CONCLUSION: These findings map the RCT landscape in cancer screening, revealing marked disparities in evidence across cancer types and identifying oral cancer as the most limited. Further RCTs are urgently needed to strengthen the evidence base and support effective oral cancer screening programs.

item.title: FGL1 Drives Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition and Cisplatin Resistance in Laryngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70545
Published: 2026-Nov-15
PMID: 43035855



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fibrinogen-like protein 1 (FGL1) is involved in tumor progression and immune regulation, but its role in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) is unclear. METHODS: Plasma FGL1 levels were measured in 120 LSCC patients and 50 controls using ELISA. Tissue expression was analyzed via TCGA-HNSC. Functional assays evaluated proliferation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, and cisplatin sensitivity. Prognostic value was assessed using survival and regression analyses. RESULTS: FGL1 was significantly elevated in LSCC plasma and tumor tissues. Functional studies showed that FGL1 promotes proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT while inhibiting apoptosis and enhancing cisplatin resistance. Mechanistically, FGL1 knockdown increased Cleaved Caspase-3 and decreased Bcl-2 expression. High FGL1 levels were associated with poorer overall survival and independently predicted prognosis. CONCLUSION: FGL1 promotes LSCC progression and chemoresistance, highlighting its potential as a circulating biomarker and therapeutic target.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of specialist palliative care (SPC) alongside immunotherapy in head and neck cancer (HNC) is unclear. METHODS: This retrospective population-based cohort study included adults with HNC who died in 2013-2021 in Alberta, Canada. The primary exposure was SPC timing (early, late, none), with immunotherapy use in the last 12 months of life as a secondary exposure. The outcome was potentially avoidable acute care use (ICU admission, 15+ hospital days, or 2+ ED visits) in the last month of life. Multivariable logistic regression was performed. CONCLUSION: Early SPC was associated with lower potentially avoidable acute care use for HNC regardless of immunotherapy use.

item.title: Donor-Site Morbidity After Buccinator Myomucosal Flap: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
item.dc:creator: Vaira LA, Massarelli O, Polesel J, Ferri A, Chiesa-Estomba CM, Acosta DF, Consorti G, Cirignaco G, Salzano G, Maglitto F, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Vaira LA, Massarelli O, Polesel J, Ferri A, Chiesa-Estomba CM, Acosta DF, Consorti G, Cirignaco G, Salzano G, Maglitto F, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71062
Published: 2026-Nov-15
PMID: 43035386



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Buccinator myomucosal flaps (BMF) are increasingly used for reconstruction of small- to medium-sized intraoral defects because they replace oral mucosa with similar tissue. However, donor-site morbidity and its determinants remain poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate donor-site morbidity after BMF harvest and identify factors associated with unfavorable outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective international multicenter cohort study was conducted across 11 centers (10 in Europe and one in India). Adult patients undergoing reconstruction with BMF after oncologic resection and a minimum follow-up of 6 months were included. Donor-site morbidity was assessed during dedicated follow-up visits using a standardized clinical scoring system evaluating mouth opening, oral commissure symmetry, vestibular restoration, cheek lining reconstruction, and cosmetic outcome. RESULTS: A total of 340 patients were included (mean age 58.6 ± 13.9 years; 50% female; mean flap area 14.6 ± 6.2 cm2). The mean donor-site outcome score was 10.7 ± 3.4. At multivariable linear mixed-effects analysis accounting for center, adjuvant radiotherapy or radiochemotherapy and donor-site closure by secondary healing were independently associated with lower scores, whereas the buccal artery myomucosal island flap and the tunnelized facial artery myomucosal island flap were associated with higher scores. Wound dehiscence was the most frequent complication (9.1%). In 223 patients with available data, higher adherence to rehabilitation exercises was associated with improved outcome scores, both with and without adjuvant radiotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: BMF provides reliable reconstruction with generally favorable donor-site outcomes. Morbidity is mainly influenced by adjuvant radiotherapy, donor-site management, flap design, and adherence to postoperative rehabilitation exercises.

item.title: Prospective comparison of CT- and MRI-based tumor delineation based on intraoperative navigation and spatially annotated pathology in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Bauer L, Kühle R, Fuchs J, Moratin J, Deng M, Ehle M, Schindehütte R, Schröter P, Stritzke F, Kozyra K, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bauer L, Kühle R, Fuchs J, Moratin J, Deng M, Ehle M, Schindehütte R, Schröter P, Stritzke F, Kozyra K, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1884392
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43065419



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Precise tumor delineation is critical for navigation-guided surgery and radiotherapy (RT) in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are both recommended for staging and provide complementary information. However, quantitative comparisons of CT- and MRI-based tumor contours remain scarce, while a spatial comparison with histopathological data has never been performed. Therefore, we prospectively compared gross tumor volumes (GTV) derived from CT and MRI before navigation-guided surgery and correlated the results with spatially annotated pathology. METHODS: This imaging sub-analysis was conducted within the prospective NAVIGATORR trial (NCT05671458). Fifteen patients with locally advanced midfacial SCC underwent contrast-enhanced CT and 1.5T or 3T MRI (T1w, T2w, DWI) for navigation-based surgery planning. Datasets were rigidly co-registered and an experienced radiologist independently contoured the GTV on CT and MRI while blinded to the other modality. Besides qualitative and volumetric evaluation, spatial agreement was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Hausdorff distance (HD). Tumor contours were correlated with spatially annotated intraoperative biopsy locations and histopathological results. RESULTS: Fifteen patients and 109 spatially annotated biopsy locations (19 tumor-positive) were analyzed. MRI was preferred for tumor delineation by the radiologist in all cases, with superior differentiation between tumor and mucosal swelling (73%) and improved soft tissue contrast (67%). MRI based GTVs were significantly larger than CT-based GTVs (median 28.3 ml vs. 16.8 ml; p = 0.02). DSC values demonstrated fair agreement with considerable heterogeneity (median 0.58; IQR 0.47-0.65), and median HD was 16 mm (IQR 12-27 mm). MRI-based contours encompassed numerically more tumor-positive biopsy locations than CT-based contours (6/19 vs. 1/19; clustered McNemar p = 0.20) while including fewer tumor-negative locations (7/90 vs. 10/90; p = 0.53). At patient level, at least one tumor-positive biopsy was located inside the contour in 3/8 (MRI) vs. 1/8 (CT) patients. DISCUSSION: GTV delineation differs substantially between MRI and CT in locally advanced midfacial SCC, and the two modalities provide complementary information. These exploratory findings support the complementary use of MRI and CT for tumor visualization. Clinical implications remain to be shown by the primary endpoint analysis of the NAVIGATORR trial.

item.title: From ancient remedy to modern use: cannabis and cannabinoids in cancer care in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Behl D, Abrams DI, Zylla DM, D'Andre SD
item.description:
Authors: Behl D, Abrams DI, Zylla DM, D'Andre SD
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1878313
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43061359



Abstract:
Cannabis, an ancient plant that has been used for millennia, is increasingly utilized by patients with cancer to alleviate symptoms related to both the disease and its treatment. This complex botanical contains multiple bioactive compounds, most notably delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD), which interact with the endogenous endocannabinoid system. THC has been studied the most, and synthetic cannabinoids are approved for the management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. However, evidence supporting cannabis for other cancer-related symptoms-including chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, insomnia, appetite stimulation, and non-neuropathic pain-remains limited. CBD alone has not demonstrated consistent or meaningful clinical benefit. Although preclinical data exist, there is no clinical evidence supporting cannabis as a cancer treatment. Cannabis may interact with prescribed medications, particularly with high-dose oral formulations, and its effects on immunotherapy are under investigation. Overall, cannabis is generally well tolerated, though adverse effects can be significant. Use is discouraged in individuals under 25 years of age due to ongoing neurodevelopment, and patients with active psychiatric or cardiovascular conditions should use cannabis only under close clinical supervision.

item.title: Association between postoperative glutamine supplementation and short-term outcomes after ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
