Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ileostomy reversal is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity despite being considered a relatively minor surgical procedure. Although glutamine supplementation has been investigated in gastrointestinal surgery, evidence regarding its role in patients undergoing ileostomy reversal remains limited. This study evaluated the association between postoperative glutamine supplementation and short-term outcomes following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with colorectal cancer who underwent elective ileostomy reversal between January 2015 and December 2025. Patients were classified into the glutamine group, who received postoperative intravenous glutamine supplementation, and the control group. Postoperative outcomes within 30 days, including complications, gastrointestinal recovery, and length of hospital stay, were compared between groups. RESULTS: A total of 183 patients were included, comprising 103 patients in the glutamine group and 80 in the control group. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 74 matched pairs were identified. Compared with the control group, the glutamine group had a significantly lower incidence of overall postoperative complications (14.9% vs. 29.7%, P = 0.043) and infectious complications (9.5% vs. 23.0%, P = 0.041). The glutamine group also had shorter times to first flatus, first defecation, and initiation of oral diets, as well as lower incidences of postoperative nausea and vomiting and abdominal distension. Hospital stay was shorter in the glutamine group. No significant between-group differences were observed in postoperative serum prealbumin, total protein, or albumin levels. CONCLUSIONS: In this PSM study, postoperative glutamine supplementation was associated with fewer postoperative complications, faster gastrointestinal recovery, and shorter hospital stay following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. These findings indicate a potential association between glutamine supplementation and favorable short-term postoperative outcomes and warrant confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

item.title: Salivary glands auto-segmentation in head and neck radiotherapy: imaging modalities, models, and clinical relevance.
item.dc:creator: Wong WL, Shum CY, Chow YL, Man KH, Law HKW, Tam SY
item.description:
Authors: Wong WL, Shum CY, Chow YL, Man KH, Law HKW, Tam SY
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1923659
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054526



Abstract:
Radiotherapy-induced salivary gland injury is a major contributor to xerostomia and impaired quality of life in patients with head and neck cancer, making accurate organ-at-risk delineation clinically important. Deep learning-based auto-segmentation has the potential to improve contouring efficiency and consistency, but reported performance is heterogeneous and its clinical significance is not always clear. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on salivary gland auto-segmentation across computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PSMA PET-CT), with particular emphasis on gland-specific challenges, performance evaluation, and clinical translation. CT has the largest evidence base and remains most relevant to routine radiotherapy planning, whereas MRI provides improved soft-tissue visualization and PSMA PET-CT offers high functional contrast for selected salivary structures. Across modalities, segmentation performance is generally more challenging for smaller structures, particularly the sublingual and tubarial gland regions. Importantly, geometric metrics such as the Dice similarity coefficient do not alone establish clinical acceptability or dosimetric equivalence; evaluation should also consider boundary accuracy, expert correction burden, clinical acceptability, and dosimetric impact. Current evidence is further limited by heterogeneous study designs and reference standards, scarce external validation, and limited evidence linking auto-segmentation directly to treatment-related toxicity or patient outcomes. Future research should prioritize multi-institutional validation, clinically meaningful evaluation, improved segmentation of small glands, and human-in-the-loop integration into adaptive radiotherapy. Overall, auto-segmentation represents a promising tool for salivary gland delineation, but its clinical implementation should be supported by evidence extending beyond geometric accuracy alone.

item.title: Radiomics-driven multimodal integration in precision radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma- current evidence, clinical barriers, and future directions.
item.dc:creator: Ma Y, Xie Y, Gou Q, Chen N, Gou Q
item.description:
Authors: Ma Y, Xie Y, Gou Q, Chen N, Gou Q
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1902266
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054349



Abstract:
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), a head and neck malignancy, is highly sensitive to radiation. Accordingly, radiotherapy has long been the primary curative modality for patients with non-metastatic NPC. Although intensity-modulated radiotherapy has significantly improved target conformality and normal tissue protection, local recurrence, distant metastasis, and late toxicity remain important issues in long-term management. To achieve a balance between tumor control and normal tissue protection, the continuous integration of multi-source information throughout the treatment workflow is critical. Radiomics has the potential to quantify spatial heterogeneity that may not be fully captured by conventional visual assessment. In this review, radiomics-driven multimodal integration refers to the task-specific combination of imaging-derived phenotypes with complementary clinical variables, Epstein-Barr virus DNA (EBV-DNA), hematological biomarkers, dose distributions, pathological features, molecular data, longitudinal imaging, or treatment-delivery information for defined radiotherapy decisions. This review focuses on the clinical timeline of precision radiotherapy for NPC and provides an overview of radiomics-driven multimodal integration studies. It discusses the current applications and limitations of this framework in pretreatment risk stratification and treatment selection, target volume and organ-at-risk definition during radiotherapy planning, on-treatment monitoring and adaptive radiotherapy, toxicity prediction and normal-tissue protection, and post-treatment recurrence assessment and re-irradiation decision-making. This synthesis of current evidence, clinical barriers, and methodological considerations may inform future validation and implementation of radiomics-driven multimodal integration in NPC precision radiotherapy.

item.title: Proton beam therapy in the treatment of adenoid cystic carcinoma of the head and neck: a single enterprise retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Rohit A, Voss M, Gunn H, Ma D, Patel S, Lester S, Rwigema JC, Neben-Wittich M, Foote R, Routman DM, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Rohit A, Voss M, Gunn H, Ma D, Patel S, Lester S, Rwigema JC, Neben-Wittich M, Foote R, Routman DM, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1968350
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054136



Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a rare salivary gland malignancy with high propensity for perineural invasion (PNI) and relative radioresistance. Proton beam therapy (PBT) may improve tumor control through improved target coverage, as well as higher physical and biologic dose while limiting dose to surrounding critical structures. This single-enterprise two-site study reports outcomes and toxicity in patients with ACC of the head and neck (HN) region treated with curative-intent PBT. METHODS: From 2015-2025, 89 patients with HN ACC were treated with curative-intent PBT. Patients with distant metastases or prior radiotherapy (RT) were excluded. Clinical outcomes were assessed retrospectively. Toxicities were recorded prospectively using CTCAE v5.0. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate local tumor control (LC), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) and overall survival (OS). Hazard ratios, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and test of association between tumor and treatment variables and outcomes were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 3.1 years. Sixty-nine patients underwent surgery followed by postoperative PBT, while 20 received definitive PBT for unresectable disease. The 3-year LC rate was 98.3% following postoperative PBT and 82.6% following definitive PBT. Treatment approach was not significantly associated with LC. Three-year DMFS was 86.2% and 64.9%, respectively, while 3-year OS was 94.4% in both cohorts. Twenty-one patients developed distant metastases, most commonly involving the lungs. Six patients experienced acute grade 3 toxicities, including dysphagia, mucositis, and dermatitis; seven experienced late grade 3 toxicities, most commonly osteoradionecrosis (n=4). One patient had both acute and late toxicity. No grade 4 or 5 toxicities occurred. CONCLUSIONS: Curative-intent PBT was associated with favorable LC and acceptable toxicity. Outcomes according to definitive versus postoperative treatment should be interpreted descriptively due to substantial baseline differences between groups and confounding by indication. Longer follow-up and larger studies are needed.

item.title: Pretreatment platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and survival after definitive radio(chemo)therapy for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: an exploratory cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Werner J, Lehnick D, Strobel K, Stenz NA, Morand GB, Rajan GP
item.description:
Authors: Werner J, Lehnick D, Strobel K, Stenz NA, Morand GB, Rajan GP
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1970136
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054093



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current staging provides limited prognostic accuracy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated whether pretreatment systemic inflammatory ratios and 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-D-glucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([18F]FDG PET/CT) metabolic parameters are associated with survival in patients treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 110 patients with HNSCC treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy at a single center. Inflammatory ratios, including the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), were derived from a pretreatment blood count. Metabolic parameters were obtained from staging [18F]FDG PET/CT. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and disease-specific survival (DSS). A Cox model comprising PLR, p16 status, cT category and age was fitted for each endpoint. Missing p16 status was handled by multiple imputation. RESULTS: A higher PLR was independently associated with worse OS (HR per interquartile range 1.61, 95% CI 1.13-2.28; p = 0.008) and DSS (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.21-2.60; p = 0.003), alongside p16-negativity. cT4 category and age were also independently associated with OS. p16 was missing in 30% of patients, mostly non-oropharyngeal tumors. Complete-case analysis was therefore restricted to 77 patients, in which the point estimates were similar, but the association no longer reached significance. PLR correlated weakly with cT category (Spearman ρ = 0.275, p = 0.004) without collinearity. In exploratory analyses, the association between a high PLR and worse survival was clear in oropharyngeal tumors but weaker in other subsites. Metabolic parameters did not demonstrate an independent association with survival after adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: Pretreatment PLR was independently associated with worse OS and DSS in HNSCC treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy in the primary multiple-imputation analysis. Effect estimates were consistent in direction and magnitude across all three approaches to missing p16 status. A higher PLR indicates a worse prognosis, but the association is modest and does not guide treatment selection. Prospective validation with prespecified cutoffs is required before clinical use.

item.title: Differences in variant profile between follicular thyroid carcinoma and adenoma: targeted next-generation sequencing study.
item.dc:creator: Lai CC, Chang TA, Chen YJ
item.description:
Authors: Lai CC, Chang TA, Chen YJ
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1902761
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43053988



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preoperative ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration cytology cannot reliably distinguish follicular thyroid carcinoma (FTC) from follicular thyroid adenoma (FTA), making these neoplasms particularly challenging to diagnose. Although several studies have explored variant differences using targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) panels, the molecular distinctions between FTC and FTA remain incompletely defined. In this study, targeted NGS was performed on DNA from 52 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded specimens. METHODS: Genomic DNA was extracted, quality assessed, and targeted NGS performed for 14 genes commonly mutated in thyroid neoplasms. Synonymous variants were excluded, and analyses then focused on pathogenic alterations. Variant frequencies were evaluated at both the locus and gene levels in FTC and FTA. RESULTS: After excluding synonymous variants, 1,074 variants across 14 genes were identified, with 92.8% clustered in five genes: TERT (70.5%), TSHR (8.6%), RET (5.9%), TP53 (4.2%), and BRAF (3.6%). FTC and FTA exhibited distinct variant landscapes, and TERT variants were significantly enriched in FTC. EIF1AX splice site variants (chrX:20148727; c.338-2A>C and c.338-2A>T) were significantly associated with FTC. In the pathogenic dataset, each additional EIF1AX variant increased the likelihood of FTC by 15.4-fold. In contrast, RET and PTEN variants were more frequent in FTA, and each additional RET variant reduced the probability of FTC by nearly half (odds ratio, 0.489). CONCLUSION: These findings underscored the potential diagnostic utility of variant profiling. TERT and EIF1AX variants were predictors of malignant transformation, whereas RET and PTEN variants were more frequently detected in FTA. Their diagnostic and therapeutic utility warrants further validation in clinical settings.

item.title: A systematic review: is contralateral elective neck dissection or neck radiotherapy indicated in lateralised cT3/T4 N0 oral squamous cell carcinoma?
item.dc:creator: Obialo N, Tagdiwala PA, Cassidy O, Schilling C, Eldweny H, Leung B, Bisase B, Norris P, Doumas SN
item.description:
Authors: Obialo N, Tagdiwala PA, Cassidy O, Schilling C, Eldweny H, Leung B, Bisase B, Norris P, Doumas SN
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1944716
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43047546



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Contralateral cervical lymph node metastasis remains a therapeutic challenge in patients with lateralised T3/T4 N0 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), with current guidelines offering differing recommendations regarding management of the contralateral neck. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from January 2008 to March 2026 for studies evaluating contralateral neck management in lateralised T3/T4 N0 OSCC. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and QUADAS-2, according to study design. Where possible, a meta-analysis was undertaken by combining outcome measures, otherwise due to anticipated heterogeneity a narrative synthesis was used. RESULTS: Search of the databases revealed 10,670 articles, following deduplication 5,173 were screened and 23 articles were sought for retrieval. Thirteen studies were included, involving 2,764 patients, predominantly retrospective cohorts; 561 were clearly identified as well lateralised T3N0 or T4N0. The tongue was the most common tumour subsite. A random-effects meta-analysis of proportions demonstrated a pooled contralateral neck disease rate of 16.1% (95% CI 1.2-51.7%), the 95% prediction interval was 0.1-90.3%, indicating substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 93.5%). Available studies did not provide sufficient evidence to determine whether elective contralateral neck treatment improves locoregional control, disease-free survival or cancer specific survival compared with observation. Interpretation was limited by retrospective study designs, heterogeneity and potential confounding. Sentinel lymph node biopsy and lymphoscintigraphy-guided approaches may help identify selected patients at risk of contralateral disease, although evidence in advanced tumours remains limited. DISCUSSION: Overall, the current evidence is insufficient to support or oppose routine elective contralateral neck dissection or radiotherapy in lateralised T3/T4 N0 OSCC. Selective lymphatic mapping may support more individualised management, but prospective validation is required before its routine use. item.title: Comparative effectiveness of five treatment strategies for locally advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma in resource-limited settings: a multinomial overlap-weighted real-world cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Song L, Chen Y, Pan Z, Ma Z, Li J, Jiang L
item.description:
Authors: Song L, Chen Y, Pan Z, Ma Z, Li J, Jiang L
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1993812
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43047457



Abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: For locally advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma (LA-OSCC), radical surgery followed by risk-adapted postoperative radiotherapy or concurrent chemoradiotherapy is standard. In resource-limited settings, limited radiotherapy access, costs, and poor tolerance yield multiple pragmatic strategies. Prior real-world studies mostly used pairwise comparisons, lacking systematic evaluation of all coexisting strategies within one framework. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 388 patients with LA-OSCC treated between January 2019 and December 2022, classified into five groups by actual treatment received: surgery with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (surgery plus CRT), surgery with adjuvant radiotherapy (surgery plus RT), surgery with adjuvant chemotherapy (surgery plus CT), surgery alone, and definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT). Multinomial overlap weighting targeting the average treatment effect in the overlap population (OW-ATO) balanced 10 baseline covariates, and overlap-weighted Cox models with robust variance estimation compared overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and disease-specific survival (DSS). Two-group (surgery versus definitive CRT) and four-group (operated patients, pathology-adjusted) analyses, competing-risk models, and sensitivity analyses (IPTW-ATE, landmark, early-death exclusion, E-value, bootstrap) assessed robustness. RESULTS: After overlap weighting, the maximum absolute pairwise standardized mean difference decreased from 0.548 to 0.168. Compared with surgery plus CRT, surgery plus RT showed no statistically significant differences in OS (hazard ratio [HR] 1.33, 95% CI 0.76-2.33), DFS (HR 1.23, 95% CI 0.79-1.90), or DSS (HR 1.56, 95% CI 0.77-3.15), whereas surgery plus CT (OS HR 2.54, 95% CI 1.47-4.39), surgery alone (OS HR 3.21, 95% CI 1.94-5.32), and definitive CRT (OS HR 3.31, 95% CI 1.97-5.57) were each associated with significantly worse outcomes across all three endpoints. Findings were consistent across all analytical layers and sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: In resource-limited real-world settings, surgery-based multimodal strategies were associated with better survival in LA-OSCC. Surgery plus RT did not differ significantly from surgery plus CRT; however, given wide confidence intervals and limited power, equivalence was not established, and it should be considered only a potential de-escalation option for selected patients who cannot receive concurrent chemotherapy-not as a replacement for standard chemoradiotherapy in high-risk disease. Surgery plus CT should be reserved as a second-best option when radiotherapy is completely unavailable.

item.title: Single-cell and spatially resolved immune profiling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a bibliometric and thematic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Li Y, Wang B, Zhang N, Peng G
item.description:
Authors: Li Y, Wang B, Zhang N, Peng G
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1985265
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43047303



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Single-cell and spatially resolved technologies have expanded research on immune heterogeneity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We examined relationships among research themes, their cited foundations, and their temporal representation. METHODS: Web of Science Core Collection and PubMed were searched for publications dated from 1900 through July 1, 2026. After deduplication and screening, 587 English-language articles and reviews were included. Bibliometric networks were analyzed using VOSviewer, R, and bibliometrix. Document-level cosine overlaps between keyword and reference clusters were evaluated using stratified permutations with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Temporal analyses used keyword proportions and citation-weighted reference-year profiles within three descriptive windows. Sensitivity analyses examined database composition, inclusion thresholds, and individual recent references. RESULTS: Publication output increased after 2021. China had the largest publication output, while the United States had the highest citation count and international-collaboration total link strength. Co-citation and keyword analyses identified four and three domains, respectively. K3-C2 had the largest observed cosine score (0.661), exceeding its null mean by 0.039 (adjusted P = 0.0072); K1-C1 also exceeded its null expectation (adjusted P = 0.0012). Among keyword-available publications, spatial transcriptomics increased from 0.0% to 1.7% and 8.3% across the three windows. The recent reference subset contained five references, all published in 2024; its C2 share was sensitive to individual references. Keyword-cluster agreement was high across database sources and moderate at the stricter occurrence threshold. CONCLUSION: The analysis identifies relationships among immune, cellular, stromal, spatial, and computational literature domains and descriptive changes in keyword representation. These findings provide a quantitative literature framework for further investigation of HNSCC immune profiling.

item.title: Targeted alpha therapy for solid tumors: biological rationale, clinical advances, and future perspectives.
item.dc:creator: Li Q, Xie J, Chen F, Li L, Yang C
item.description:
Authors: Li Q, Xie J, Chen F, Li L, Yang C
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.2007300
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041765



Abstract:
Targeted alpha therapy (TAT) delivers high-linear-energy-transfer radiation over a few cell diameters and is being explored for resistant and microscopic solid-tumor disease. This targeted narrative review evaluates alpha-emitting platforms and clinical evidence by tumor type and development stage, with a focused literature update through 12 October 2026. Unlike broader radiochemistry-centered reviews, we place approved, randomized, early-phase, observational, and preclinical findings in separate evidence tiers. Radium-223 dichloride has randomized survival evidence in symptomatic bone-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, whereas molecularly targeted actinium-225, lead-212, astatine-211, and thorium-227 agents remain investigational in the indications discussed. Updated examples include the 2026 ACTION-1 actinium-225-DOTATATE dosimetry substudy, the 2026 first-in-human astatine-211-MABG study, 2025 lead-212-DOTAMTATE phase II disclosures, and a negative 2025 mesothelin-targeted thorium-227 study. Quantitative outcomes are reported with their study design and limitations rather than interpreted as indirect head-to-head comparisons. Major barriers include isotope supply, incomplete daughter retention, salivary, marrow, and kidney toxicity, spatially heterogeneous target uptake, and uncertainty in patient-specific microdosimetry. We propose practical, imaging-led selection and a priority-ranked translational roadmap.

item.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging: a mini review of current applications and future directions.
item.dc:creator: Lotfian G, Ginat DT
item.description:
Authors: Lotfian G, Ginat DT
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.2010320
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041688



Abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new opportunities to enhance medical imaging in pediatric oncology through quantitative image analysis and clinical decision support. This mini review examines the emerging role of AI in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging, including applications in lesion detection and characterization, tumor segmentation and volumetric analysis, treatment planning, longitudinal surveillance, prognostication, and precision medicine. Particular attention is given to the challenges of translating these approaches to pediatric populations, where rare and heterogeneous tumors, limited datasets, variable imaging protocols, and insufficient multicenter validation remain important barriers. We also discuss emerging strategies that may facilitate clinical translation, including federated learning, multimodal data integration, explainable AI, and integration with existing radiology workflows. Although pediatric-specific evidence remains limited, continued multicenter collaboration and prospective validation may enable AI-based tools to provide more reproducible quantitative imaging assessment and increasingly personalized clinical decision support. Ultimately, the clinical value of these technologies will depend on their ability to augment radiologist expertise and improve patient care through responsible integration into routine practice.

item.title: Long-term outcomes of globe-sparing surgery combined with adjuvant radiotherapy for lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Zhao SX, Xu WQ, Zhao XH, Su D, Li YY, Ma R, Hei Y, Mu XT, Yang XJ
item.description:
Authors: Zhao SX, Xu WQ, Zhao XH, Su D, Li YY, Ma R, Hei Y, Mu XT, Yang XJ
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1934640
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041427



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term outcomes of radiotherapy after globe-sparing surgery for lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) and compare different radiotherapy protocols. METHODS: This retrospective comparative case series included 97 patients with LGACC treated with globe-sparing surgery followed by postoperative radiotherapy between November 2003 and April 2023. Patients received one of four protocols differing in clinical target volume (CTV) expansion and radiation dose. Primary outcomes included locoregional recurrence, distant metastasis, locoregional recurrence-free survival (LRFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), progression-free survival, and overall survival. RESULTS: The median age was 38 years, and median follow-up was 7.2 years. The overall 5-, 10-, and 15-year LRFS rates were 80.2%, 74.5%, and 74.5%, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified R2 resection (HR = 4.16, 95% CI: 1.53‑11.35, P = 0.005), cribriform histology (HR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.08‑0.81, P = 0.020), and smaller CTV expansion (≤0.5 cm; HR = 4.06, 95% CI: 1.41‑11.67, P = 0.009) as independent predictors of local recurrence. Patients treated with ≤0.5-cm CTV expansion and ≤54 Gy had significantly lower 5-, 10-, and 15-year LRFS rates (55.2%, 40.5%, and 40.5%) than those treated with 1-cm CTV expansion and 60-80 Gy (90.5%, 90.5%, and 90.5%; P < 0.001). DMFS did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.599). Best-corrected visual acuity of 20/20-20/40 was preserved in 35.1% of patients. The 5-year risk of radiation retinopathy was 25.1% and 43.6% (P = 0.057) in the no extended-margin and extended-margin groups, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Radiotherapy with 1-cm CTV expansion and a dose of 60 Gy after globe-sparing surgery provided favorable locoregional control for LGACC. Distant metastasis remained the predominant cause of treatment failure.

item.title: TMSB10 marks a malignant epithelial programme spatially associated with fibroblast-matrix niches in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Yao B, Tang Y, Liu S, Nie X, Lin L, Xu Q
item.description:
Authors: Yao B, Tang Y, Liu S, Nie X, Lin L, Xu Q
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1969309
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43041408



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malignant epithelial states at the tumour-stroma interface may contribute to local invasion in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), but their reproducibility across patients and spatial relationship with fibroblast-matrix niches remain unclear. METHODS: Single-cell transcriptomes from 16 untreated OSCC samples were analysed to localise TMSB10 and derive a TMSB10-associated invasion-related programme (TIP) through within-patient comparisons of aneuploid epithelial cells. Frozen TIP scores were evaluated in independent single-cell and spatial cohorts. Spatial associations were tested using adjusted generalised additive models and random-effects meta-analysis. Survival associations were examined in GSE41613 and TCGA-HNSC, and TMSB10 was silenced in HN6 and HN30 cells. RESULTS: Among 89, 323 cells, TMSB10 was highly expressed in epithelial and endothelial compartments. TMSB10-high aneuploid epithelial cells exhibited 1, 569 differentially expressed genes and enrichment of 16 Hallmark pathways related to proliferation, oxidative metabolism, and epithelial plasticity. Frozen TIP scores showed concordant directions across patients and in GSE103322. TIP-core and TIP-anchor were positively associated with cancer-associated fibroblast/extracellular matrix (CAF/ECM) scores in all 18 spatial sections, with pooled effects of 0.1434 and 0.1456, respectively (both FDR = 0.000402); this association was reproduced in all four GSE220978 patients. In GSE41613, higher TMSB10 expression was associated with poorer overall and disease-specific survival after clinical adjustment, whereas TCGA-HNSC showed no consistent adjusted association. TMSB10 knockdown reduced CCK-8 signals, wound closure, and Transwell migration in both cell lines. CONCLUSION: Within malignant epithelial cells, TMSB10 expression is associated with a reproducible, pEMT-related programme spatially associated with CAF/ECM-rich regions. Knockdown findings support the involvement of TMSB10 in OSCC cell growth and migration.

item.title: FIXED: A CAD/CAM Tooth-Bonded Device for Intermaxillary Fixation in Orthognathic Surgery Patients Treated With Clear Aligners.
item.dc:creator: Sáez F, Mariscal J, Victoria C, Toledo X
item.description:
Authors: Sáez F, Mariscal J, Victoria C, Toledo X

Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 43051268



Abstract:
Clear aligner therapy poses a particular challenge for orthognathic surgery: the absence of fixed orthodontic attachments compromises conventional intermaxillary fixation, which relies on brackets or skeletal anchorage. We describe FIXED, a CAD/CAM-designed, tooth-bonded intermaxillary fixation device for patients undergoing orthognathic surgery during clear aligner therapy. The device is digitally planned from intraoral scans, 3-dimensional-printed in biocompatible resin, and cemented to the buccal enamel before surgery, providing anchorage for wires and elastics without the morbidity of skeletal screws or the esthetic compromise of temporary brackets. We illustrate the digital workflow, fabrication protocol, and surgical application in 3 patients with Class II and Class III malocclusion, one of them managed with a surgery-first protocol. In all cases, intraoperative fixation was achieved as planned, with no device-related complications during the perioperative period.

item.title: Is the Duration of Antibiotic Prophylaxis Associated With Severe Surgical Site Infection, Length of Hospital Stay, and Hospitalization Charges After Cleft Lip and/or Palate Surgery?
item.dc:creator: Nishida T, Ono S, Oshima S, Tsuda Y, Watanabe H, Matsui H, Fushimi K, Yasunaga H, Hoshi K
item.description:
Authors: Nishida T, Ono S, Oshima S, Tsuda Y, Watanabe H, Matsui H, Fushimi K, Yasunaga H, Hoshi K
Journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons | DOI: 10.1016/j.joms.2026.10.008
Published: 2026-Oct-30
PMID: 43039029



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite widespread antibiotic prophylaxis in cleft lip and/or palate surgery, the frequency of severe surgical site infection (SSI) requiring debridement or reoperation and the optimal duration of prophylaxis remain uncertain. Large-scale, real-world evidence is needed to better inform antibiotic prophylaxis strategies in this population. PURPOSE: To estimate the frequency of severe SSI and measure the association between antibiotic prophylaxis duration and postoperative outcomes across cleft lip and/or palate procedures. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, SAMPLE: This nationwide, multicenter, retrospective cohort study used the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination inpatient database (April 2012 to March 2022). Patients undergoing cleft lip and/or palate surgery were screened, and those with immunocompromised status, preoperative antibiotic use, or no antibiotic prophylaxis were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: Duration of postoperative antibiotic prophylaxis (short term: ≤ 2 days vs prolonged: ≥ 3 days). MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLE(S): The primary outcome was the frequency of severe SSI, defined as SSI requiring debridement or reoperation during the same hospitalization. The secondary outcomes were length of hospital stay and hospitalization charges. COVARIATES: Age, sex, body mass index, anesthesia duration, procedure category, comorbidities at admission, and teaching hospital status. ANALYSES: Multivariable regression models were used to evaluate associations between prophylaxis duration and outcomes. Subgroup analyses were performed for the 4 surgical procedure groups. The frequency of severe SSI was summarized descriptively. A P value < .05 was considered statistically significant. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dentofacial deformities can affect jaw function, oral health-related quality of life, and psychological well-being. Longitudinal evidence assessing multiple patient-reported outcomes remains limited. PURPOSE: To measure temporal changes in 6 patient-reported outcomes following bimaxillary orthognathic surgery. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, AND SAMPLE: This prospective longitudinal cohort study included consecutive adults with skeletal Class III dentofacial deformity who underwent bimaxillary surgery at Ondokuz Mayıs University between October 2024 and June 2025 and were followed for 6 months postoperatively. Patients with skeletal Class I or II deformity, clinically significant facial asymmetry requiring additional procedures, revision surgery, or American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status II or higher were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLE: The predictor was assessment time: 1 week preoperatively (T0), and 6 weeks (T1), 3 months (T2), and 6 months (T3) postoperatively. Lower scores indicate less symptom burden (FAI), functional limitation (JFLS-8), oral behavior frequency (OBC), adverse oral health impact (OHIP-14), anxiety symptom severity (GAD-7), or depressive symptom severity (PHQ-9). No single primary outcome was prespecified. COVARIATES: Age and sex. ANALYSES: Friedman tests and Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (P < .0083) evaluated temporal changes. Secondary generalized estimating equation models adjusted for age and sex. RESULTS: All 37 participants completed follow-up (mean age, 20.9 ± 2.3 years; 26 female [70.3%]). Abstract:

item.title: Peripheral glia drive the initiation of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Micheli S, Salas-Bastos A, Huỳnh K, Cecconi V, Kolm I, Vasilevska J, Debbache J, Renz PF, Diener J, Gwerder M, et al.

Authors: Micheli S, Salas-Bastos A, Huỳnh K, Cecconi V, Kolm I, Vasilevska J, Debbache J, Renz PF, Diener J, Gwerder M, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78778-1
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 43052304



Abstract:
Although tumor innervation is known to promote cancer progression, underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood and have mostly been linked to axonal signaling. Here, we identify peripheral glia as critical drivers of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), the second most common skin cancer in humans. Tumor-associated glial cells (TAGs) resemble embryonic Schwann cell lineage stages, are abundant in the stroma of premalignant lesions and established murine and human cSCC, and are essential for tumor formation. TAG activation in premalignant lesions is triggered by UV-induced anti-inflammatory macrophages, which in turn are polarized by TAGs into pro-tumorigenic FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, key components of the cSCC microenvironment. Consequently, TAG depletion reduces FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in keratinocytes, thereby impairing cSCC initiation by disrupting intercellular communication required for tumor development. As most solid tumors are innervated and harbor peripheral glia, our findings reveal TAGs as regulators of tumor initiation with potential relevance beyond skin cancer.

item.title: Large-scale proteomic characterization reveals clinically relevant subtypes of early-stage papillary thyroid cancer for prognostic prediction.
item.dc:creator: Pan J, Ye F, Yao Y, E W, Wang Y, Wu X, Wen S, Zhang Y, Ju F, Chen M, et al.

Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78559-w
Published: 2026-Oct-20
PMID: 43052258



Abstract:
Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) has a rising incidence. The majority are diagnosed at an early stage, albeit with a minority exhibiting aggressive tendencies. Given its generally indolent nature, controversy persists regarding the management of early-stage PTCs, particularly surgical intervention and long-term surveillance strategies. Here, we conduct a large-scale proteomic characterization of early-stage PTC based on tumor samples from 797 patients. Proteomic profiling unveils clinically relevant modules and identifies six subtypes, capturing the spectrum of heterogeneity from indolent to progressive disease states. Notably, subtypes associated with higher progression risk display enhanced signatures of ribogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Furthermore, integrating machine learning with protein co-expression network analysis, we identify predictive markers of PTC progression risk such as GPX3 and TMSB4X. Integration of clinical and proteomic data provides a valuable resource for  a deeper understanding of early-stage PTC biology and may inform personalized management strategies for patients with indolent or progressive disease.

item.title: Short-term effectiveness and impact of Vaxchora vaccine during the 2024 cholera outbreak in Mayotte.

Published: 2026-Oct-19
PMID: 43045698



Abstract:
Global cholera resurgence and vaccine shortage have driven the adoption of reactive one-dose strategies with killed oral cholera vaccines (OCVs). The live-attenuated vaccine CVD 103-HgR (Vaxchora) shows high efficacy in human challenge studies, but its real-world effectiveness in outbreaks is unknown. Here, we analyze the 2024 outbreak in Mayotte, focusing on Koungou village, which had high cholera incidence and vaccine uptake. We develop several stochastic models and calibrate them to daily cases by vaccination status. In total, 3354 individuals (71%) of Koungou's at-risk population (n = 4733) received CVD 103-HgR, and 77 cases were confirmed, with symptom onset between 19 April and 7 July 2024. At baseline, we estimate a basic reproduction number R 0 of 1.5 (95% credible interval (CrI): 1.2, 1.9) and a CVD 103-HgR effectiveness in preventing cholera of 87% (95% CrI: 74, 99), remaining between 75% and 91% across scenarios. Counterfactual simulations estimate 536 (95% CrI: 240, 824) cases averted at baseline, with a range of point estimates from 152 to 1228 across sensitivity analyses. Rapid single-dose CVD 103-HgR deployment is associated with high effectiveness during a real‑world outbreak, with a substantial but more uncertain population impact, supporting the inclusion of live-attenuated OCVs in reactive strategies when necessary.

item.title: Baseline radiographic and microbiologic predictors of treatment outcomes in a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB.
item.dc:creator: Shen EQL, Mpinda S, Maama L, Tamirat M, Sebakeng P, Oyewusi L, LaHood A, Trevisi L, Romo M, Osso E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Shen EQL, Mpinda S, Maama L, Tamirat M, Sebakeng P, Oyewusi L, LaHood A, Trevisi L, Romo M, Osso E, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78700-9
Published: 2026-Oct-17
PMID: 43052337



Abstract:
WHO-endorsed shortened, all-oral regimens have improved tolerability and outcomes for MDR/RR-TB treatment, but predictors of poor outcomes remain incompletely-characterized. We conducted a prospective cohort study (NCT05871489) of adults with bacteriologically-confirmed pulmonary MDR/RR-TB treated with a shortened, all-oral regimen in Lesotho. We evaluated baseline microbiologic and radiographic features and their associations with time-to-culture-conversion, end-of-treatment outcomes, and final post-treatment outcomes. Among 238 participants (median age 41 [IQR:31-56], 29% female, 62% with HIV), there were 27 unfavorable outcomes (20 deaths, 3 treatment failures, 4 recurrences). 142 of 148 (95.9%) with positive baseline cultures experienced conversion within four months. Fibrosis, cavitation, bilateral disease, and high smear grade were associated with delayed culture conversion and lower odds of treatment success. Bilateral disease was more strongly associated with unfavorable outcomes in those without HIV; fibrosis and high smear grade showed stronger associations among those with HIV. Cavitation with high smear grade (uOR=0.29, 95%CI:0.11-0.78; aOR=0.39, 95%CI:0.14-1.14), and severe fibrocavitary disease (multi-lobar fibrosis and at least one cavity ≥5 cm) (uOR=0.20, 95%CI:0.07-0.64; aOR=0.26, 95%CI:0.07-0.94) were negatively associated with favorable final outcomes. These findings suggest that baseline sputum and chest radiographic features-particularly in-combination-identify higher-risk patients and may inform risk-adapted strategies for shortened all-oral MDR/RR-TB regimens.

item.title: Epitope-resolved Epstein-Barr virus antibody mapping identifies disease-stratifying signatures in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Yu Y, Fei Z, Huang W, Liu M, Tang J, He Q, Wang S, Li F, Zheng C, Xie H, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Yu Y, Fei Z, Huang W, Liu M, Tang J, He Q, Wang S, Li F, Zheng C, Xie H, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78818-w
Published: 2026-Oct-17
PMID: 43039919



Abstract:
Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects most adults worldwide and usually persists without symptoms, yet in some individuals it is associated with malignancies such as nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). How antibody responses to specific regions of EBV proteins differ between healthy individuals and patients with NPC remains incompletely understood. Here we show that epitope-resolved profiling of EBV antibodies reveals serological patterns associated with NPC development and clinical outcomes. We developed EBVScan, a quantitative phage-display platform covering 42 EBV isolates, to map IgA and IgG responses across the viral proteome. Multi-centre validation identified an antibody response to the TK139-194 region that distinguished NPC from controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.97. We also identified antibody-reactive regions enriched in healthy individuals that overlapped known viral receptor-interaction interfaces, and selected peptides from these regions reduced EBV infection in vitro. In patients with NPC, baseline antibody signatures were additionally associated with chemotherapy response and progression-free survival. Together, these findings provide an epitope-resolved view of EBV-host immune interactions and identify serological features with potential applications in NPC detection and patient stratification.

item.title: Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans.
item.dc:creator: Oerlemans J, Alejandro RJ, Hemelsoet D, Genbrugge E, Bouche K, Defreyne L, De Herdt V, Holroyd CB

Abstract:
The reward positivity (RewP) is an event-related brain potential (ERP) component associated with feedback and goal completion. Although the component is said to be generated in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), this inference is disputed because of the inverse problem. Recent intracranial electroencephalogram (EEG) current source density analyses provided direct evidence that the RewP is generated in caudal ACC, specifically Brodmann areas 24c' and 32'. To further test this hypothesis, we examined the effects of damage to frontal cortex damage on RewP amplitude. Scalp EEG was recorded from 68 stroke patients with frontal lesions while they performed a trial-and-error guessing task used to elicit a canonical RewP. Non-parametric voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping revealed that damage to Brodmann areas 24c' and 32' significantly attenuated RewP amplitude. item.title: Fluke-borne viruses are a risk factor and diagnostic target for diseases caused by carcinogenic trematodes.
item.dc:creator: Chaiyadet S, Roblin T, Fauchois A, Temmam S, Hing D, Jacquemet E, Bigot T, Li B, Kende J, Capai L, et al.

Authors: Chaiyadet S, Roblin T, Fauchois A, Temmam S, Hing D, Jacquemet E, Bigot T, Li B, Kende J, Capai L, et al.
Journal: Nature communications | DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78561-2
Published: 2026-Oct-16

Abstract:
Three trematode parasites, Schistosoma haematobium, Opisthorchis viverrini, and Clonorchis sinensis are recognized group 1 carcinogens for their roles in squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder and bile duct cancer (cholangiocarcinoma). We aimed to assess the presence of fluke viruses and their association with malignancy in fluke infections. We showed that all three carcinogenic trematodes harbored related viruses. Focusing on O. viverrini, we observed virus persistence at discrete life stages and viral tropism for the fluke tegument, and we provided molecular and serological evidence of parasitized hosts' exposure to viral RNA and proteins. Serological analyses confirmed seroconversion of residents in endemic sites and revealed that antibody titers and avidity against fluke-borne viruses increase in individuals with hepatobiliary diseases. Random forest models discriminated efficiently between liver-fluke-infected participants without disease and those with periductal fibrosis or cholangiocarcinoma. Thus, we show that fluke-borne viruses are risk factors and diagnostic targets for fluke-associated cancer.

item.title: Impact of CT image co-registration on dosimetric verification in ¹²⁵I seed implantation for lung cancer.
item.dc:creator: Ke X, Huimin Y, Hongtao Z, Guohui C, Xiaoli L, Jinxin Z, Zezhou L, Juan W
item.description:
Authors: Ke X, Huimin Y, Hongtao Z, Guohui C, Xiaoli L, Jinxin Z, Zezhou L, Juan W
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16797-3
Published: 2026-Sep-18
PMID: 43046208



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the accuracy and differences between a pre-operative and intra-operative CT image co-registration-based dosimetric verification method and the conventional verification method in ¹²⁵I seed implantation for lung cancer. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 30 lung cancer patients who underwent ¹²⁵I seed implantation at our center between January 2021 and December 2024. Histopathological types included squamous cell carcinoma (9 cases), adenocarcinoma (13 cases), and other tumors (8 cases). All patients received a prescription dose of 140 Gy, with seed activities of 0.73 ± 0.99 mCi. All patients underwent both image co-registration-based dosimetric verification (hereinafter referred to as the co-registration group) and conventional immediate post-operative dosimetric verification (hereinafter referred to as the Conventional Group). In the co-registration group, preoperative contrast-enhanced CT images were imported into the 3D Treatment Planning System (3D-TPS), followed by the last intraoperative non-contrast CT scan. Rigid co-registration of the two CT datasets was performed within TPS, and the target volume was manually delineated on the fused images. In the Conventional Group, the last intraoperative non-contrast CT was directly imported into the TPS, and the target volume was manually delineated on these images. Following target delineation in both groups, seeds were identified and postoperative dose-volume histograms (DVHs) were generated using the TPS to obtain dosimetric parameters, including target volume (Vol), postoperative D₉₀ (minimum dose covering 90% of the target volume), V₉₀, V₁₀₀, V₁₅₀, and V₂₀₀ (representing the percentages of the target volume receiving 90%, 100%, 150%, and 200% of the prescription dose, respectively). Follow-up chest CT scans were performed at 1-6 months postoperatively. Treatment response was evaluated using the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1, with short-term efficacy and adverse reactions documented. Paired t-tests were used to analyze differences in dosimetric parameters between each verification group and the preoperative plan, as well as between the Co-registration and Conventional Groups. Bonferroni correction was applied for post hoc multiple comparisons to examine statistical significance between groups. RESULTS: All procedures were successfully completed, with treatment outcomes including 5 cases of complete response (CR), 14 cases of partial response (PR), 9 cases of stable disease (SD), and 2 cases of progressive disease (PD), while no adverse reactions or grade 3 or higher complications were observed. Normality testing confirmed that the target volume (Vol) and all dosimetric parameters from the 30 patients were normally distributed. Statistical comparisons revealed significant differences in Vol, D₉₀, V₁₅₀, and V₂₀₀ between the conventional post-operative verification group and the pre-operative plan, whereas the image co-registration group showed significant differences only in V₁₅₀ and V₂₀₀ compared to the pre-operative plan. A significant difference in Vol was also found between the conventional and co-registration verification groups. Bonferroni-corrected post hoc tests demonstrated a statistically significant difference in D₉₀ between the pre-operative plan and the conventional verification group, but not with the co-registration group, while significant differences in V₁₀₀ and V₂₀₀ were observed between the pre-operative plan and both verification groups, with no significant differences detected in Vol, V₉₀, or V₁₀₀. CONCLUSION: Dosimetric verification using the image co-registration method demonstrates significantly improved stability in D90 values compared to the conventional post-operative verification approach when evaluated against the pre-operative plan, suggesting its potential as a novel option for medical physicists in post-implant dose verification.

item.title: A preliminary nomogram for risk stratification of oral candidiasis in patients with diabetes mellitus: a real-world study.

Journal: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oooo.2026.08.019
Published: 2026-Sep-02

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop a clinical nomogram for assessing the probability of oral candidiasis (OC) for risk stratification in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). RESULTS: Of the 314 patients, 174 (55.4%) had OC and 140 (44.6%) did not. Multivariable analysis identified 5 predictors: denture wearing (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.92, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.87-27.70), oral hygiene status (aOR 1.66, 95% CI 1.05-2.61), fasting blood glucose (aOR 1.37, 95% CI 1.05-1.77), age (aOR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), and male (aOR 0.57, 95% CI 0.33-0.97). item.title: Oral HPV prevalence and its associations with HIV, oral health, immune function, and behavioral factors among youth and mothers in Nigeria: a cross-sectional study.
item.dc:creator: Kumar A, Peter O, Osagie E, Chen J, Akhigbe P, Liu J, Idemudia NL, Kavecky P, Obuekwe O, Udoko FEE, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Kumar A, Peter O, Osagie E, Chen J, Akhigbe P, Liu J, Idemudia NL, Kavecky P, Obuekwe O, Udoko FEE, et al.
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-29077-3
Published: 2026-Aug-28
PMID: 43058613



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: People living with HIV (PLWH) are more susceptible to human papilloma virus (HPV) infection; however, data on the oral HPV burden among youth with or without perinatal HIV exposure or infection in sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce. This study described the distribution of oral HPV and examined demographic, dental, immune and behavioral characteristics of youth and mothers across HIV exposure groups in Nigeria and explored characteristics that co-occurred with oral HPV DNA detection. METHODS: This baseline cross-sectional analysis leveraged data from a prospective cohort in Nigeria. At study enrollment, mothers were categorized as either HIV-infected (HI) or HIV-uninfected (HU), while youth participants were classified as HIV-infected (HI), HIV-exposed uninfected (HEU), or HIV-unexposed uninfected (HUU). Standardized questionnaires were used to capture behavioral data, and comprehensive dental examinations were used to assess decayed, missing, and filled teeth (DMFT), oral hygiene index simplified (OHIS), and gingival inflammation score (GIS). Oral rinse specimens were tested for oral HPV DNA and blood samples were collected for immune parameter assessment (CD4/CD8). The analysis was primarily descriptive given the small number of participants with oral HPV DNA detection. No inferential statistics were performed for HPV-stratified comparisons. RESULTS: In our study, the overall oral HPV prevalence was low and was detected in 7/671 (1%) youth and 8/404 (2%) mothers. Among youth, oral HPV DNA was predominantly detected in HI and HEU groups and exclusively among HI mothers. In descriptive comparisons, youth with HPV DNA tended to have higher CD4 and lower CD8 counts and differences in oral health indices, whereas mothers with HPV DNA reported earlier sexual debut and lower CD4 counts. No inferential statistics were applied to these subgroups. These observations are hypothesis-generating given the small number of participants with detectable HPV DNA. CONCLUSIONS: Despite its low prevalence, oral HPV was detected predominantly among PLWH and co-occurred with certain dental and immunological characteristics in this small number of cases. These findings highlight oral health as a potential area of interest in the context of oral HPV DNA detection and support further investigation into the relationships among oral health, the immune response, and viral detection within the HIV care setting in sub-Saharan Africa but cannot establish causal or predictive relationships.

item.title: Investigating the effect of an educational intervention based on the Health Belief Model in reducing dental plaque among sixth-grade elementary students.

Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-29201-3
Published: 2026-Aug-27
PMID: 43058638



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Implementing programs that develop personal skills and promote adherence to oral health behaviors is essential for adolescents. Therefore, this study was conducted to determine the effect of an educational intervention based on the Health Belief Model (HBM) in reducing dental plaque among sixth-grade elementary students. METHODS: This quasi-experimental study was conducted with 80 sixth-grade students in Urmia, Iran. The students were divided into two groups: an intervention group and a control group, each consisting of 40 participants. The data collection tool consisted of three parts: questions pertaining to demographic information; a researcher-developed questionnaire assessing HBM constructs and knowledge regarding dental plaque and behaviors associated with its reduction; and an assessment of the level of dental plaque using the O'Leary Plaque Index. During one month, the intervention group participated in three 45-minute training sessions focused on oral hygiene instructions. Data were collected in two phases: before the educational intervention and three months afterward. RESULTS: The post-intervention mean scores in the intervention group were as follows: knowledge (7.92 out of 11), perceived susceptibility (21.55 out of 25), perceived severity (36.70 out of 40), perceived benefits (39.85 out of 45), self-efficacy (43.92 out of 50), cues to action (33.80 out of 40), and behaviors related to reducing dental plaque (50.07 out of 60). These findings indicate significant increases in all these measures in the intervention group after the educational program, compared to both their baseline scores and the control group (p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: The findings of this study suggest that educational interventions based on the HBM can be a valuable strategy for promoting oral health behaviors and reducing dental plaque among sixth-grade students. It is recommended that the educational intervention developed in this study be used as a simple and effective approach to encourage oral health behaviors and reduce the burden of preventable oral diseases, in conjunction with other routine school health care practices.

item.title: Behavioral and structural determinants of HPV vaccination among adult men in China: a qualitative study using the COM-B model.
item.dc:creator: Cai Y, Ding C, Ren X, Li M
item.description:
Authors: Cai Y, Ding C, Ren X, Li M
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-28931-8
Published: 2026-Aug-26
PMID: 43058592



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is recommended for both males and females; however, uptake among adult men in China remains low. Understanding behavioral and structural determinants may inform gender-neutral HPV prevention strategies. METHODS: This qualitative study used semistructured interviews and reflexive thematic analysis guided by the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model. Data were collected in February 2026 at a tertiary hospital health examination center in Qingdao, China. A purposive sample of 25 adult men aged 18-45 years attending routine health examinations was recruited. Interviews explored knowledge of HPV, attitudes toward vaccination, relational influences, and interactions with health services. Recruitment continued until data saturation was achieved, defined as the point at which no new themes or concepts emerged from successive interviews. RESULTS: Among 25 participants (mean [SD] age, 31.5 [5.8] years; 14 [56%] married), 20 (80%) had heard of HPV, 4 (16%) knew that men could receive HPV vaccination, and 2 (8%) had been vaccinated. Three themes were identified. First, HPV was commonly framed as a women's health issue, limiting men's perceived susceptibility and reducing self-initiated motivation for vaccination. Second, vaccination motivation was often relationally mediated, with participants reporting willingness to vaccinate when encouraged by partners. Third, opportunity-related structural barriers, including limited clinician recommendation and perceived vaccine cost, constrained translation of vaccination intentions into behavior. CONCLUSIONS: HPV vaccination decisions among Chinese adult men appear shaped primarily by motivational determinants, supported by limitations in HPV-related knowledge and perceived susceptibility, as well as opportunity-related structural barriers within the health system. Interventions to increase uptake may benefit from de-gendered public health communication strategies that move beyond the "cervical cancer vaccine" framing, alongside stronger clinician engagement and efforts to reduce structural barriers.

item.title: Association of P53 and P16 expression with surgical and oncologic outcomes in vulvar squamous cell carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Salameh E, Kassis NE, Tarchichi S, Chakra RA, Khalil K, Yazbek D, Atallah D
item.description:
Authors: Salameh E, Kassis NE, Tarchichi S, Chakra RA, Khalil K, Yazbek D, Atallah D
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16792-8
Published: 2026-Aug-24
PMID: 43052862



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this research is to evaluate the relationship between p53 and p16 expression and various clinicopathologic features, surgical interventions, and oncologic outcomes in patients diagnosed with vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC). METHODS: We carried out a retrospective cohort study involving women treated for vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (FIGO stages I-IV) at Hôtel-Dieu de France in Beirut, Lebanon, from 2014 to 2024. Collected data included patient characteristics, surgical management, postoperative complications, pathological features, recurrence, and survival rates. Tumor specimens were analyzed for p53 and p16 expression using immunohistochemistry, and human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA was evaluated by vaginal PCR. Statistical analyses included Chi-square, Fisher's exact, and Mann-Whitney tests, with significance set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: A cohort of 125 patients was initially included in the analysis, of whom 86 underwent p53/p16 immunohistochemical evaluation: 38 were p53-positive, 15 were p16-positive, 33 were p53/p16-negative,14 out of 86 patients were HPV positive. In the p53-positive group, tumors were more often central, resulting in clitoral excision in all patients in this subgroup (p = 0.008). P53 positivity was associated with increased rates of inguinal lymph node metastasis (p < 0.001) and a higher number of metastatic lymph nodes excised (p = 0.001), and worse baseline Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance score (p = 0.04). Although depth of invasion tended to be greater in p53-positive tumors, this difference was not statistically significant. Postoperative complication rates, recurrence, and survival were comparable across biomarker groups. No significant association was observed between p16 expression, HPV status, or smoking history. CONCLUSION: In our cohort, p53-positive vulvar squamous cell carcinoma was associated with more aggressive clinicopathologic features, including increased nodal involvement and wider surgical resection due to midline tumor location. However, p53 expression was not associated with higher postoperative complication or recurrence rates. These findings suggest that while p53 may reflect tumor aggressiveness; its role in guiding surgical or prognostic decision-making requires further prospective evaluation.

item.title: Treatment outcomes and immuno-nutritional biomarkers in patients with cervical esophageal squamous cell carcinoma treated with induction chemotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Ono T, Nakata Y, Chitose SI, Sueyoshi S, Kurita T, Sato F, Murotani K, Kawaguchi T, Oka T, Mitsuhashi T, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Ono T, Nakata Y, Chitose SI, Sueyoshi S, Kurita T, Sato F, Murotani K, Kawaguchi T, Oka T, Mitsuhashi T, et al.
Journal: BMC cancer | DOI: 10.1186/s12885-026-16820-7
Published: 2026-Aug-24
PMID: 43052838



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical esophageal squamous cell carcinoma arises below the upper esophageal sphincter, often causing dysphagia due to tumor progression. Therefore, some patients with cervical esophageal squamous cell carcinoma become malnourished. Due to its low incidence, limited information is available on prognostic immune-nutritional biomarkers. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 47 patients with resectable cervical esophageal squamous cell carcinoma who underwent induction chemotherapy. Prognostic biomarkers were selected based on their 5-year area under the curve values. The association between the biomarkers and disease-free survival or overall survival was evaluated in univariable and multivariable analyses. RESULTS: The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index and high-sensitivity modified Glasgow prognostic score were significantly associated with the induction chemotherapy response. Both the C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index and the high-sensitivity modified Glasgow prognostic score were significantly associated with disease-free survival and overall survival in univariable analysis. C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte indices were significantly associated with disease-free survival and overall survival in multivariable analysis. CONCLUSION: The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index is a useful prognostic treatment outcome biomarker in patients with cervical esophageal squamous cell carcinoma undergoing induction chemotherapy.

item.title: An outbreak report of Influenza A(H3) among residents of a large nursing home in northern Italy: attack rates, clinical features and outcomes.
item.dc:creator: Fonda F, Faruzzo A, Bellini G, Provenzano A, Lampis E, Brunelli L, Marzinotto S, Pipan C, Curcio F, Privitera G, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Fonda F, Faruzzo A, Bellini G, Provenzano A, Lampis E, Brunelli L, Marzinotto S, Pipan C, Curcio F, Privitera G, et al.
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-28934-5
Published: 2026-Aug-21
PMID: 43064999



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nursing homes are high-risk settings for Influenza outbreaks, and the 2025-2026 Influenza season has been characterised by an earlier-than-usual epidemic onset globally with the emergence of a novel Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K strain including mutations that were not present in the strains of the 2025-2026 seasonal vaccine. Detailed outbreak investigations are essential to inform Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) strategies in these high-risk yet often neglected settings. METHODS: This is an outbreak report originating from data collected within an ongoing prospective surveillance in a 375-bed publicly funded nursing home in northern Italy. Surveillance for acute respiratory infection (ARI) was applied to all residents enrolled in the study (November-December 2025). Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from all ARI cases and analysed for Influenza A(H3). Cases were defined as residents with ARI and laboratory-confirmed Influenza A(H3). Attack rates (ARs), case-hospitalisation rate (CHR), and case-fatality rate (CFR) were calculated with 95% confidence intervals. Findings are here reported according to the Outbreak Reports and Intervention Studies of Nosocomial infection (ORION) guidelines. RESULTS: Of 217 involved residents (median age 88 years, 83% Influenza vaccinated), 50 (AR = 23%; 95% CI 17.6-29.2) had laboratory-confirmed Influenza A(H3). Fever (89.8%) and cough (81.6%) were the predominant symptoms. Median symptom duration was 3 days (range 1-14 days). The CHR was 8% (4/50; 95% CI 2.2-19.2) and the CFR was 0.0% (0/50; 95% CI 0.0-7.1) among confirmed cases. CONCLUSIONS: This outbreak of Influenza A(H3) documented an overall attack rate slightly below the published median for nursing home outbreaks, with a low CHR and no confirmed deaths among laboratory-confirmed cases. The outbreak commenced in week 48, earlier than the historical Italian epidemic onset, underscoring the need for proactive surveillance, sustained attention to Influenza vaccination and IPC measures in long-term care facilities even ahead of the traditional winter peak.
